card.failure_class: Silent structural malformation of a dispatch brief — a missing safety marker (worktree isolation, dispatch-id, mandatory snippet) fails not at authoring but silently and downstream (agent edits main, lifecycle can't track it, agent trips a sharp edge mid-run); recurs on every launch and compounds across a concurrent fleet.
card.engineering_obligation: Verify the instruction packet that confers autonomy before granting it — any work order that launches an autonomous actor must be structurally validated at the point of no return, deterministically, not by probabilistic review.
card.solution_structure: A deterministic pre-dispatch lint over the brief text (marker-presence battery; genre-gated content checks so precision checks fire only where the brief's declared genre requires them), wired into the canonical dispatch path as a required prepare step: exit 1 refuses the launch and rolls back dispatch state.
card.guarantee: No agent launches from a structurally malformed brief. Boundary: well-formedness only — a fully-marked brief can still be mis-scoped; scoping judgment stays human. Human-only audited bypass exists.
card.semantic_level: dispatch artifact ⊨ launch contract — the brief's declared marker/snippet set conforms to the schema of what makes a launch safe; the check governs the work order, not the work.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Structure ≠ correctness (green lint buys marker coverage, not a good brief). Authoring tax unless a template pre-places markers by construction. Every new marker is a lint↔template drift edge. Content checks false-positive without genre gating — a lint tuned out is worse than one not written. The bypass env var is a real hole.
card.dependencies: Mandatory-snippet registry (agent/governance-doc-controls/mandatory-snippet-table) as the enumerable check source; a dispatch wrapper as the sole launch path; a brief-template generator; complements dynamic-context-injection (content side) and role-typed-dispatch (policy side).
card.known_uses: DocAble's agent_prompt_lint.py battery; the isolation:worktree marker as a BLOCKING check; the dispatch-id-token + on-disk marker-file joint check; the agent-brief starter template.
card.likely_parent_family: Validated dispatch (admission gate on the work order itself — pre-authorization of autonomous work)

card.failure_class: Governing knowledge scattered across hundreds of docs: agents re-derive invariants badly or violate cross-file rules they never found; every doc added makes any single fact less findable; 'the docs say so' is unenforceable because no agreed place holds the rule.
card.engineering_obligation: Maintain one bounded, canonical, authoritative map of the rules that govern the system, shared by every actor as boot context — canonicality (one home per rule) and boundedness (scannable size) mechanically held.
card.solution_structure: A stable-numbered rule index loaded into every agent's boot context; each rule is a one-line statement cross-referencing exactly one canonical deep doc; a cap/bloat lint bounds size and a conformance lint holds the cross-reference discipline; a self-describing admission test keeps local rules out.
card.guarantee: Every agent boots with the same minimal rule map; index size and cross-reference integrity are lint-held. Boundary: the index content is advisory to the agent (soft); semantic drift of a doc body under its summary is uncaught.
card.semantic_level: rule → exactly-one canonical home (the index ⟷ doc-corpus canonicality relation), plus fleet-context ⊇ index (guaranteed shared availability of the map).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Per-invocation context tax paid by every dispatch — bounded only because the cap lint exists. Keeping the index small pushes detail back into pull-model sub-docs (the regress dynamic-context-injection answers). Cross-refs rot semantically even when links hold. Admission is judgment-heavy; a lint bounds size, not worth.
card.dependencies: Doc-hygiene lints (cap + coverage); stable-numbering convention; the canonical-deep-doc discipline; consumed by dynamic-context-injection as a registry; same artifact as claude-md-rule-index viewed from the dispatch-context lens.
card.known_uses: DocAble's CLAUDE.md numbered rule index (booted into every agent); the repository documentation index with one-line summaries; the three-part earns-its-spot admission test.
card.likely_parent_family: Governed knowledge base (documentation as enforced infrastructure)

card.failure_class: Constraint under-specification at dispatch: an agent lacking the tacit which-rules-apply-here mapping makes plausible edits that violate governing rules, then burns rounds discovering and repairing them downstream where authoring context is gone ('pinball'); multiplies across concurrent agents.
card.engineering_obligation: Deliver the constraints that govern an action to the actor at the point and moment of action — convert policy from available (pull, optional) to binding (pushed into the mandatory task specification).
card.solution_structure: A slicing operator over file-addressable, self-documenting constraint registries, run in two directions: forward (files → governing constraints, injected into the brief at authoring or pulled via CLI) and reverse (diff line-ranges → findings this change introduced, powering CI self-heal). One adapter per registry.
card.guarantee: None hard in the forward direction — injection raises salience and shifts odds; downstream gates still guarantee. The reverse direction gives deterministic attribution of introduced findings (no snapshot cache, no staleness).
card.semantic_level: change-target → governing-constraint — the relevance relation ('which of the hundreds of documented rules govern these files'), externalized from the engineer's head into a computable mapping.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Garbage-in: value bounded by constraint declarations having scope tags and actionable fix-hints. Advisory — an agent can ignore an injected rule. The relevance operator has real precision/recall failure surface (over-injection floods and lowers salience; under-injection silently omits). Per-registry adapter maintenance.
card.dependencies: File-addressable constraint registries (lint fleet scope tags, component-zone model, banned-API list, test corpus, doc index) read via meta-model-consumption; the brief-authoring injection point; counterpart: reflection-facet-substrate (feed-back twin over the same policy source).
card.known_uses: DocAble's constraint-extraction tool (forward slicing); the diff-line-range attribution machinery behind CI self-heal; consumption of the component-zone model and lint scope tags as addressable registries.
card.likely_parent_family: Point-of-action policy delivery (feed-forward constraint injection)
card.note: Flagship entry; the generalization ('every meta-substrate becomes a just-in-time constraint registry once you add a slicing operator') reads as a canonical-pattern claim in its own right.

card.failure_class: Correlated per-dispatch decisions (which LLM, worktree vs main, permission mode, applicable gates) drift apart when re-made ad hoc under load: wrong-tier output ships, a commit agent runs where its hook can't fire, a resource-hungry agent triggers the gate it should never touch; recurs on every dispatch, invisible until damage.
card.engineering_obligation: Bind correlated authority and capability decisions into a single declared type, fixed once at dispatch and enforced at every gated operation — policy-by-type, not per-instance judgment.
card.solution_structure: A small closed role enum, each role mapping to a policy tuple (LLM · isolation · permissions · gate set); a sole dispatch wrapper sets the role; downstream enforcers read the ambient role declaration and refuse operations that don't match it.
card.guarantee: An agent's exercised capabilities mechanically match its declared role (gated ops refuse mismatches). Boundary: the role makes the choice legible and enforceable, not correct — a mis-routed task still ships wrong-tier work; audited human bypass exists.
card.semantic_level: actor → authority profile — every gated operation ⊨ the dispatcher's declared role type; a closed vocabulary over bundles of authority.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A closed enum is rigid: a task fitting no role forces a mis-fit or a new role. The role leaks as ambient environment state into subprocesses and needs special-casing (the build-pool exception). Declaring ≠ matching the work. Bypassable via the audited escape.
card.dependencies: A role registry (closed enum + tuples); per-operation enforcers reading the role env var; the sole dispatch wrapper; consumers: pre-commit hook (commit-slave shaped so the hook fires), aggregate-compute-protection's role gate.
card.known_uses: DocAble's four roles (sonnet-active / opus / lint-runner / commit-slave); the aggregate-lint runner's refusal of sonnet-active; commit-slave operating on main without isolation; the build-pool must-not-export-role edge.
card.likely_parent_family: Closed action vocabulary (applied to agent authority: typed authority profiles)

card.failure_class: Sequential integration of concurrent agent work serializes the fleet and thrashes on conflicts: each merge risks colliding with the last, throughput collapses toward one-at-a-time, and hot-spot files stall everything behind them; recurs every merge tick, worsens with fleet size.
card.engineering_obligation: Integrate concurrent independent work at fleet throughput with conflict-freedom established by construction before landing, not discovered by retry.
card.solution_structure: Per tick: build a conflict graph (worktrees as nodes, a shared file as an edge) from per-worktree file footprints; compute a (greedy) maximum independent set; land that set together, defer the rest. Upstream, dispatch discipline composes waves with disjoint footprints so the independent set is large. Landed commits verified by patch-id/ancestry reachability.
card.guarantee: A landed batch is conflict-free by construction — no two members touch the same file. Boundary: the set is greedy, not provably maximum; a mis-declared footprint can admit a real conflict; hot-spot files cap the batch at 1 regardless of algorithm.
card.semantic_level: change-set ⟂ change-set — pairwise independence (file-footprint disjointness) over concurrent work, proved before integration.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Greedy approximation. Hot-spot files hard-cap throughput — the win depends entirely on dispatch-side footprint disjointness, so the mechanism moves complexity upstream into scheduling. Footprint declaration becomes a trusted input.
card.dependencies: Known per-worktree footprints; the agent-registry (which worktrees are ready); disjoint-footprint dispatch planning; patch-id reachability checks.
card.known_uses: DocAble's merge_train.py conflict-graph batcher; the disjoint-footprint wave-composition recipe; verify-cherrypick-reachability patch-id checks.
card.likely_parent_family: Staged admission gates (integration tier) — conflict-aware integration scheduling
card.note: The directive's exclusion list names MIS batching as the exemplar of 'clever but distracts' (admire-the-implementation risk); 3b should weigh whether the durable idea is 'independence proved before integration' with MIS as one implementation.

card.failure_class: Broken changes flowing past the cheap moment: without a commit-time gate a break surfaces at the expensive stairs (merge-train, deploy) where authoring context is gone and one unchecked commit can poison a whole merged batch; recurs on every commit, compounds with fleet size.
card.engineering_obligation: Run the cheapest sufficient checks at the earliest boundary, and make their passing an independently verifiable fact bound to the exact artifact state — downstream stages must be able to check, not trust, that upstream gates fired.
card.solution_structure: A three-stanza commit hook (changed-file-scoped lints → unit-tier tests → tree-sha-keyed marker write) plus a downstream merge-check verifier that refuses any agent commit lacking a valid marker for its tree; explicit audited bypass prefixes and a reasoned skip marker for codemod waves; --no-verify banned for agents.
card.guarantee: No agent commit advances to merge unless the cheap checks passed on exactly this tree (tree-sha keying prevents a pass on one tree vouching for another). Boundary: bypass-prefix commits skip by design (auditable, honesty-dependent); only cheap-tier coverage.
card.semantic_level: artifact state → verified evidence — 'checks ran green on THIS tree' as a deterministic, replay-proof fact rather than a trust assumption; the first rung of a cheap-before-expensive gate ordering.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Per-commit latency is a direct incentive to bypass — a slow unit tier erodes cadence and pressures the escape hatches. Bypass prefixes are a real audited hole. The tree-sha marker logic is subtle: keying drift either blocks good commits or vouches for the wrong tree.
card.dependencies: Fast changed-file-scoped lints; a seconds-fast unit tier (the 1-second-rule discipline); a marker store keyed to tree identity; the merge-check verifier (without it markers are advisory); role-typed dispatch (commit-slave shaped so the hook fires).
card.known_uses: DocAble's 3-stanza .githooks pre-commit; the worktree merge-check marker verification; the pre-commit-skip:<reason> codemod marker; the Commit-of i/N trailer requirement.
card.likely_parent_family: Staged admission gates (the path-to-production staircase) — the tree-keyed marker element is kin to re-derived-evidence patterns

card.failure_class: An agent dispatched into a subtly broken substrate (missing marker, wrong branch, empty submodule) works 30–60 minutes and then fails at commit or produces unlandable work — the failure is invisible until the end, so its cost is the entire dispatch budget; recurs whenever substrate drifts between dispatch and consumption.
card.engineering_obligation: Verify environmental health at the earliest observable moment on the production path, so a doomed run is aborted at minute one instead of discovered at minute sixty — bound the waste of work that can never land.
card.solution_structure: A health check hung on the agent's first commit: cheap total predicates over the substrate (worktree root matches, per-agent marker exists, branch is the expected one, CWD under worktree) with a clean abort path; a boot-time self-check sibling brackets the window; new checks land AUDIT-ONLY and are promoted to BLOCKING after clean sessions.
card.guarantee: Enumerated substrate failures surface at t≈0 on the real dispatch path (not a pin-test in isolation). Boundary: it only catches what it asserts — a failure mode absent from the predicate list still slips to t=60.
card.semantic_level: runtime environment ⊨ dispatch-time contract — the substrate the agent actually runs in matches what dispatch declared and the lifecycle substrate records.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Hand-maintained predicate set. A false abort kills a healthy agent — hence the AUDIT-ONLY→BLOCKING confidence-buying migration. Small latency on every agent's first commit.
card.dependencies: The agent-registry's checkable lifecycle facts (markers, branches); a detectable first-commit moment; a clean abort path; sibling: the boot-time dispatch self-check.
card.known_uses: DocAble's sentinel first-commit check; the boot-time assert-agent-canonical-dispatch self-check; the audit-only-first landing discipline for new substrate checks.
card.likely_parent_family: Fail-fast environment validation (early substrate-health gate; a stair of the staged admission staircase)

card.failure_class: An ungated deploy puts a regression directly in front of users — the failure is the incident; at agentic velocity deploys are frequent and agent-initiated, so every un-gated bad build multiplies exposure.
card.engineering_obligation: Expose no user to an unverified build: verification escalates through progressively expensive stages on traffic-free surfaces before promotion, and a predictably doomed deploy is never even started.
card.solution_structure: A pipeline of escalating gates: pre-launch predicate (lints green, no live flaky class, changed-since-main green) → build → canary revision taking no production traffic → smoke against the canary URL → promote on green → revision GC; heartbeats emit liveness through the long phases.
card.guarantee: Promotion to production is refused until smoke passes on a traffic-free canary. Boundary: only as strong as the smoke suite; a drifted canary/smoke path gives false confidence.
card.semantic_level: release candidate ⊨ observed-behavior contract before user exposure — verification precedes traffic, ordered cheap-to-expensive.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Real build-minute cost (the pre-launch predicate exists to not spend it on doomed deploys). Smoke ≠ full coverage. The gate infrastructure itself can drift (don't validate via untested infra). Each stage adds deploy latency.
card.dependencies: Canary capability (traffic-free revision); a meaningful smoke suite; promotion/rollback/GC primitives; pre-launch green signals; deploy-heartbeats for liveness.
card.known_uses: DocAble's deploy driver (canary tag → smoke → promote → GC); the pre-deploy launch predicate; per-phase deploy heartbeats.
card.likely_parent_family: Staged admission gates (deploy tier)
card.note: Entry itself flags it as standard practice with thin novelty (defense-in-depth, amplified by agentic deploy frequency) — a demotion candidate per exclusion criterion 2.

card.failure_class: Governance that doesn't bind and doesn't last: conventions living in heads or stale wikis never reach a fresh agent, and a living rules document either bloats until nothing in it lands or drifts from the canonical docs it summarizes — both taxing or misleading every dispatch, continuously.
card.engineering_obligation: Govern the document that carries the governance: the delivery vehicle for every converted failure must itself be budgeted, admission-gated, and mechanically enforced, or the whole failure→mechanism move rots at its root.
card.solution_structure: A stable-numbered rule index loaded into every agent's boot context (binding by construction); a three-part earns-its-spot admission predicate plus a router that relocates failing rules to sub-docs/comments; a hard counterpart of two blocking lints — a cap/bloat lint on size and a rule-conformance lint on the one-canonical-doc cross-reference discipline.
card.guarantee: The index's form is mechanically held: bounded size, intact cross-references, stable citable numbering. Boundary: presence ≠ obedience — the index can claim a discipline that has quietly rotted, which is exactly what the Epic DoD's re-run audits.
card.semantic_level: governance corpus → bounded binding index — the meta-relation: the record of the mechanisms is itself under mechanism (governance-of-governance).
card.forces_tradeoffs: A hard budget means perpetual triage — admitting a rule eventually evicts one, and the eviction call is judgment-heavy. Stable numbering accretes dead entries forever. The per-dispatch context tax is simultaneously the benefit (binding) and the price.
card.dependencies: A boot-context loader; the cap + conformance lints (doc-hygiene family); the Epic DoD as the claims-audit counterpart; consumed by dynamic-context-injection as the corpus it slices; same artifact as docs-hierarchy under the dispatch-context lens.
card.known_uses: DocAble's CLAUDE.md numbered rule index; the governance-doc bloat lint and rule-conformance lint; the 'what belongs in this file' self-governing meta-section; the CLAUDE-starter.md portable download.
card.likely_parent_family: Governance-of-governance (the meta-mechanism: the enforced governance document)
card.note: Deliberately double-listed with agent/context-and-dispatch/docs-hierarchy — two lenses on one artifact; 3b should treat them as one mechanism with two views.

card.failure_class: Docs drift in ways a diff doesn't show: a hand-edit to a generated file is silently overwritten, a new doc never enters the index and is unfindable, a cross-reference dangles after a move — and agents then trust the stale corpus as ground truth.
card.engineering_obligation: The structural properties of a documentation corpus (indexed, provenance-declared, reference-intact) must be mechanically checked — review sees the words, not the wiring the words hang on.
card.solution_structure: A lint family over the corpus: an index-coverage lint (every doc indexed), an autogen-provenance lint (every emitted tracked file carries its emitter + regen path in its first lines, targets registered, marker re-emitted every run), and cross-reference/link-resolution lints; new lints land AUDIT-ONLY and migrate to BLOCKING.
card.guarantee: Docs are indexed, provenance-headed, and reference-resolvable, or the pipeline fails. Boundary: mechanical only — a well-formed, well-indexed, wrong document passes.
card.semantic_level: doc corpus ⟷ its declared structure — index ⊇ docs; emitted file → declared emitter; pointer → resolvable target.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Structure, never prose correctness. The autogen registry and header convention are upkeep surfaces. Legitimate exceptions need an escape hatch (a small hole). Flipping to BLOCKING before the corpus is clean wedges the pipeline.
card.dependencies: A doc index; the autogen-targets registry + provenance convention; an exemption escape; flagship sibling claude-md-rule-index; the same read-at-lint-time move as meta-model-consumption.
card.known_uses: DocAble's index-coverage lint; the autogen-provenance lint + _AUTOGEN_TARGETS registry; the cross-reference/link lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Drift/parity gates (applied to the documentation corpus rather than a typed model)

card.failure_class: Free-form planning artifacts omit exactly the incident-preventing sections: the design doc that skips second-order dynamics ships a substrate that deadlocks at T+100, the Epic without a DoD is 'done' by assertion, the topic-introducing design without an observability block leaves the substrate unmonitorable.
card.engineering_obligation: The required analytic content of a planning artifact is a structural contract — the shape declared like a schema and materialized by scaffold, not remembered by the author under time pressure.
card.solution_structure: Fixed section-templates for the two planning genres (Epics, design docs); a stub tool atomically materializes the sections and registers the effort; lints/gates assert the required sections (registration, DoD criteria, an observability block for topic-emitting designs, a second-order-dynamics block for concurrent substrates).
card.guarantee: Section presence is enforced; an effort can't be framed without its required analytic slots. Boundary: the hollow-section hole — a presence check passes an empty 'second-order dynamics' heading; the template forces the section, not the thought in it.
card.semantic_level: planning artifact ⊨ required-section schema — the plan's shape as a typed contract, with each required section earning its place from a named past incident.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Hollow sections pass. Template + scaffold + lint must move together or drift yields false rejections. Over-templating trivial changes adds ceremony authors route around.
card.dependencies: The stub/scaffold tool; section-presence lints; the Epic DoD as the closing counterpart that verifies the template was satisfied; feeds the dynamics and observability disciplines at design time.
card.known_uses: DocAble's Epic template + epic_stub.py materializer; the observability-block rule for event-bus topics; the second-order-dynamics section rule; the EPIC-TEMPLATE and design-doc starter downloads.
card.likely_parent_family: Schema-governed planning artifacts (typed artifact shape — kin to validated dispatch, one genre up)

card.failure_class: Premature or false close of a multi-dispatch effort: accumulated claims (phase markers, 'lints pass', pin counts) rot as sibling work churns the substrate underneath, so an effort closes with defenses that no longer hold (empirically 7/7 self-marked-DONE Epics had gaps).
card.engineering_obligation: Establish completion by independently re-derived evidence against the current state — never by recorded assertion; trust nothing that was written down before now.
card.solution_structure: A close gate that (a) machine-checks every cited commit is reachable from main by ancestry or patch-id (logged override for exceptions), and (b) mandates a fresh reviewer re-run of every owned pin test and lint at HEAD, compared against the claims, plus a scan for dropped follow-ups and doc rot; on clean close, status fields rewrite atomically and the effort moves to the closed tree.
card.guarantee: An effort cannot close unless its commits are verifiably landed and its owned checks re-verified against the substrate as it stands now. Boundary: an under-declared 'owned' set re-runs too little and can still close on a rotted-but-unlisted defense; the override is a logged hole.
card.semantic_level: completion claim ⊨ re-derived evidence at current state — completion moves from assertion to recomputation.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Deliberately expensive (a strong reviewer plus a full owned-check pass) because a false close costs more. The override exists for legitimately-unreachable commits but is a way past the check. Accuracy of the owned set is load-bearing.
card.dependencies: A machine-checkable close tool; a per-effort registry of owned pins/lints; a follow-up routing mechanism; counterpart to claude-md-rule-index (form-lints vs claims-audit).
card.known_uses: DocAble's epic_close.py close --commits/--override; the Epic template's multi-criterion DoD with the Final-Opus trust-nothing re-run; the close-time tag routing-audit.
card.likely_parent_family: Re-derived definition of done (canonical pattern)

card.failure_class: Per-dispatch boilerplate omissions: an author who forgets the PATH export, commit-cadence, worktree-discovery, or submodule snippet ships an agent that trips exactly that sharp edge mid-run; which snippets are mandatory is tribal knowledge that drifts as snippets accrete.
card.engineering_obligation: The universal safety preamble for delegated work must be a registry with a mechanical reader — a checklist with no reader catches nothing.
card.solution_structure: An include-table registry (snippet → include-when condition → grep-able marker string) plus verbatim snippet bodies; the pre-dispatch brief lint greps for every required marker per the include-when spec and refuses dispatch on any absence.
card.guarantee: No brief dispatches without the required snippet markers present. Boundary: the marker catches absence, not staleness — an updated registry body doesn't propagate into already-pasted briefs.
card.semantic_level: work order ⊇ registry of universal obligations — the brief's content ⊨ the declared set of always/conditional safety boilerplate.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Verbatim-include means propagation drift. Every new snippet is a registry row + lint marker + template thread that must move together. Over-inclusion bloats briefs into noise.
card.dependencies: brief-linting as the consumer (this registry is its enabler); the snippet bodies directory; the brief-template generator that pre-places markers.
card.known_uses: DocAble's agent-snippet include-table (61 snippet files with include-when conditions); always-include snippets (worktree-path, rebase-first) vs conditional ones.
card.likely_parent_family: Validated dispatch (the enabling registry behind the work-order gate)

card.failure_class: Incident-time improvisation: under pressure an agent re-derives a response from first principles and gets the sharp edges wrong — a flailing reset destroys landed work, a naive restart re-enters the loop, a 'cleanup' removes a live worktree; the cost peaks exactly when time is shortest.
card.engineering_obligation: Pre-reason each recurring operational situation once, when nothing is burning: encode the trigger, the ordered steps, and the reflexes to avoid, and make the procedure discoverable at the moment of need.
card.solution_structure: A library of situation-keyed procedures, each naming its triggering situation, ordered response steps, and anti-pattern reflexes; cross-referenced from the terse rule index and from the substrate signal that triggers it, so the observability surface carries 'which playbook to open'.
card.guarantee: None — soft: a playbook aims the response and cannot block; its leverage is discoverability plus habit.
card.semantic_level: operational situation → prescribed response — encoded judgment keyed by the situation, not by the doc.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Ignorable. Rots when the substrate changes — a stale playbook actively mis-directs, worse than none. Dead weight once a failure mode retires. Not a substitute for designing the recurrence out or gating it.
card.dependencies: Event-bus signals as entry points (a playbook with no signal is never triggered); rule-index cross-references for discoverability; a human who reasoned the response once.
card.known_uses: DocAble's event-bus observability playbook; the cron-recovery chicken-and-egg procedure; the cron-alerts-gate recovery playbook; deploy-failure symptom→cause tables; the op-playbook starter download.
card.likely_parent_family: Encoded operational judgment (runbooks/playbooks)

agent/governance-doc-controls/operator-r.title: Operator runbook skill (positive map + symptom index, ref-lint-kept)

card.failure_class: The operator re-derives the substrate's shape from scratch every session and re-derives recoveries badly mid-incident, while doc pointers silently rot and send the next operator on a chase — the 'pet' stance (chatting the fleet toward a goal) at a scale that demands cattle.
card.engineering_obligation: Give the operator an operator-keyed map that leads with how the substrate works when healthy (the positive model) and falls back to symptom-keyed routing when it breaks — generated from a typed source of truth and kept honest by reference validation, since a non-executable index earns trust from a ref-check, not tests.
card.solution_structure: A loadable skill in two halves: a portable operating stance (observability-first RCA, the standing freedom to propose governance improvements) and a project catalog generated from typed YAML — the positive lifecycle map, symptom→resolving-doc rows, and runbooks whose steps carry typed automatability kinds (runnable / carried-brief / surface-to-user); a reference-validity lint resolves every pointer's file AND heading anchor; a partner failure-interpretation skill routes recurrences to designed mechanisms, never inline fixes.
card.guarantee: Every listed pointer resolves against disk (hard). Boundary: the skill routes, it cannot execute or block; symptom coverage is soft and rots unless incidents are appended.
card.semantic_level: observed symptom → resolving procedure, over a substrate ⟷ positive-operational-model relation; each runbook step ⊨ its declared automatability type.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Value depends on being loaded and heeded. The lint guarantees validity of listed pointers, not completeness of the listing. Anchor resolution catches more rot but fires on every heading rename. The YAML→markdown render adds a build step that can itself drift.
card.dependencies: A typed YAML source of truth; the reference-validity lint (the drift-parity move applied to a doc-skill); operational-playbooks underneath as the failure half; semantic-level-enforcement for placing designed mechanisms.
card.known_uses: DocAble's operate-ada-tool-repo skill (pointer catalog + runbook catalog YAML); typed step-kinds; the DoD drift-audit runbook whose runnable steps are driven off the system models; the file+anchor reference lint.
card.likely_parent_family: Encoded operational judgment (generated, lint-kept operator map over the runbooks)
card.abstract_name: Generated operator map with validated references

agent/governance-doc-controls/semantic-l.title: Enforce at the right semantic level

card.failure_class: A mechanism placed below its property's legibility scope silently never enforces: it either can't see the property (a leak is a call sequence, invisible one syscall at a time) or false-fires on legitimate partial state (per-commit model-parity rejects every mid-task commit) — and the mis-placement looks wired and runs green forever.
card.engineering_obligation: Place each control at the smallest scope where its property is decidable — match the mechanism's enforcement window to the property's semantic window; convenience (cheapest, earliest hook) and legibility are different axes.
card.solution_structure: A design-time placement procedure: state the property as a predicate sharp enough that 'where is this legible?' has an answer; find the smallest window containing the evidence; bind the mechanism to the lifecycle rung whose window matches, on an escalating ladder (syntactic diff-check → reasoning pass over the diff → whole-worktree final commit → agent-return review → effort-close intent review); prefer the lowest sound rung.
card.guarantee: None — a soft design-time judgment; a mis-placed mechanism still ships. The tell of a skipped placement question is a mechanism that fires forever and never catches its class.
card.semantic_level: property's legibility scope ⟷ control's enforcement scope — the meta-relation of placement itself (this entry governs where other mechanisms sit).
card.forces_tradeoffs: The higher rung costs latency — the price of soundness, not a defect. Nothing forces the question to be asked. Over-placing a file-legible property up the ladder buys nothing and delays the catch.
card.dependencies: A ladder of enforcement points at distinct scopes (commit hook, runtime events, agent-return, effort-close); a design-review or failure-interpretation path that forces the placement question; it places pre-commit-hook, lifecycle-hooks, and the Epic DoD as rung instances.
card.known_uses: DocAble's model-drift check at agent-return rather than the commit hook; the data-exfiltration/semantic-gap example (sequence, not syscall); operator-loop omissions at runtime events; the banned-API counter-example that belongs at the bottom rung.
card.likely_parent_family: PRINCIPLE candidate (L1) — this is a placement judgment that explains where mechanisms sit, not a pattern entry at the same level as its neighbors; 3b should consider lifting it out of the pattern set.

card.failure_class: Unsafe reclaim of live work: liveness inferred from filesystem timestamps races with running agents — an agent mid-work looks identical to a stale one and has its worktree destroyed under it; recurs on every cleanup pass.
card.engineering_obligation: Destructive lifecycle decisions must consult an authoritative recorded fact of liveness and state, never an inference from side effects — the record precedes the reclaim.
card.solution_structure: An append-only registry log plus a fast per-agent marker cache, dual-written by every lifecycle tool at every transition; destructive-op gates query a three-gate chain (registry → marker → git-lock) before removing anything; a declared winner (registry) on any divergence.
card.guarantee: 'Is this agent live?' is a lookup against a recorded fact, and tools refuse to operate on an agent whose live marker exists. Boundary: exactly as strong as the weakest writer — one side-door lifecycle mutation that skips the registry reintroduces the race.
card.semantic_level: destructive operation ⊨ recorded lifecycle state — authority over 'what is alive' moves from inferred filesystem signals to an authoritative append-only record.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Universal dual-write discipline is the fragile load-bearing assumption. Append-only growth needs rotation. Registry/cache divergence can briefly mislead a cache-trusting tool.
card.dependencies: The dispatch wrapper's prepare step (the first writer); consumers: tombstone-commits (live guard), cleanup-stale, merge-train (readiness), sentinel-first-commit (substrate facts).
card.known_uses: DocAble's agent-registry.jsonl + active-agents marker cache; the 3-gate cleanup-stale chain; the live-worktree guard and dedup-via-registry pattern; it concretely replaced the mtime heuristic that destroyed in-flight work.
card.likely_parent_family: Authoritative lifecycle state (record-before-destructive-action)

card.failure_class: The un-warranted change: a landed diff whose reason survives only as tribal knowledge — behavioral RCA of 'why did the fleet do this?' becomes guesswork, and any causal claim about whether a mechanism changes behavior reduces to Goodhart-able co-occurrence.
card.engineering_obligation: Every state-changing action must carry a trace to its cause, drawn from a closed taxonomy, minted at the cause and asserted at admission — causation wherever an artifact holds the cause, an honestly-labeled proxy where none can, and never a rate anyone optimizes.
card.solution_structure: A closed caused-by taxonomy (scheduled effort / runtime reflection firing / ad-hoc); the commit gate asserts the typed field is present and names a taxonomy value; the cause-id travels with the dispatch so the field comes out for free rather than being reconstructed; a _proxy suffix labels inferred causes; a telemetry query reports the mix as a health signal that is read, never rewarded.
card.guarantee: No agent commit lands without a typed cause naming a known value (presence is hard). Boundary: the choice among values is the agent's judgment (soft); proxy-labeled causes are honest inference, not causation.
card.semantic_level: every repository change → its cause — agent-side change provenance; a continuously-emitted traceability matrix, one row per commit.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Some causes are irreducibly proxy — heavier mechanism relocates rather than removes that uncertainty. The taxonomy is a coordination point (new causes need declared values). The moment the deterministic-vs-proxy ratio becomes a target, the field starts lying.
card.dependencies: The pre-commit hook as the assertion gate; dispatch artifacts that carry the cause-id; the closed taxonomy; counterpart mutator-stamps (product-side provenance); specializes the measured-leash yield query from correlation to causation.
card.known_uses: DocAble's caused-by: epic:<id> | reflection:<fire_id> | ad-hoc field asserted by the code-agent pre-commit hook; the caused-by-mix telemetry query read by a self-operations runbook.
card.likely_parent_family: Caused-by provenance (the agent-side member of the provenance stack)

card.failure_class: Dispatching new work onto a known-broken substrate: the orchestrator can see (or miss, or ignore) a high-severity alert and keep piling work into a system that cannot land it, compounding the mess.
card.engineering_obligation: A surfaced critical health failure must compel a response before new work is admitted — promote the observability signal into a blocking admission barrier (availability → binding, applied to alerts).
card.solution_structure: An append-only alert channel with a severity scale plus an ack log with terminal states; the dispatch-side tools (dispatch, worktree creation, merge-train run/stage/attest, brief creation) consult it and refuse while an unresolved HIGH exists; the canonical resolution is an alert-resolving dispatch that auto-acks and ships the fix; EXEMPT tools + the resolve path give designed-in deadlock freedom.
card.guarantee: Once polled, no new work-dispatch proceeds past an unresolved HIGH alert. Boundary: inherits the alert producer's severity accuracy; the audited bypass ack can paper over a real break; seeing the alert depends on the session-start poll discipline.
card.semantic_level: new-work admission ⊨ acknowledged substrate health — the health state of the environment becomes a precondition on admitting more work into it.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A stuck or unackable alert can wedge the orchestrator (mitigated by EXEMPT paths + recovery playbook). Mis-tagged severity over- or under-blocks. The gate is only as good as the poll that surfaces it.
card.dependencies: typed-event-bus (alerts are derived events); the ack log; dispatch tools wired to consult; a recovery playbook; the resolves-alert dispatch path.
card.known_uses: DocAble's cron-alerts channel + acks log; the HIGH-alert dispatch block across dispatch/worktree/merge-train/brief tools; the --resolves-alert auto-ack dispatch.
card.likely_parent_family: Health-conditioned admission (an observability signal promoted into a blocking gate)

card.failure_class: A hung long-running operation is indistinguishable from a slow one: the orchestrator either kills a healthy-but-slow deploy or waits forever on a dead one; process-alive proves nothing (a deadlocked process is alive).
card.engineering_obligation: Long-running operations must emit periodic progress evidence — liveness and phase advancement observable mid-flight, so staleness is decidable from signal absence.
card.solution_structure: A phase-structured operation emits phase + elapsed on a fixed cadence (every 30 s) to a greppable log; a stale-worker sweep flags emitters that stopped; a blocking startup concurrency guard sits beside the signal.
card.guarantee: Liveness and progress are observable at cadence granularity; 'no heartbeat for N windows' reads deterministically as stale. Boundary: liveness ≠ correctness — a deploy can heartbeat steadily while failing.
card.semantic_level: running operation → periodic progress assertion — absence of the expected signal ⊨ staleness; the observed distinction is progressing vs existing.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The consumer must know the cadence or the signal is noise. 30 s resolution misses short hangs. Heartbeat lines add log volume.
card.dependencies: A phase loop with an emit point; a parseable format; a cadence-aware consumer; layers under staged-deploy-gates as its liveness signal.
card.known_uses: DocAble's [heartbeat] phase=X elapsed=Ns deploy emissions; the overlapping-deploy startup guard; the stale-worker detection sweep.
card.likely_parent_family: Fleet observability surfaces (progress-liveness variant)

card.failure_class: Operator-loop omissions at predictable runtime moments (ending a turn with work queued, compacting without a hand-off, opening a session without reading alerts, editing outside the sanctioned worktree): no source artifact exists for a lint, and recall-based house-rules fail exactly when attention is thin.
card.engineering_obligation: A step owed at a runtime moment must fire deterministically at that moment, independent of anyone's memory — split enforcement into guaranteed firing (hard) and a payload that either blocks or aims (hard block vs soft guidance).
card.solution_structure: Scripts bound to named runtime lifecycle events (turn-stop, pre-compaction, session-start, before-a-tool-call); a blocking payload vetoes the action, a guidance payload re-injects text into the agent's context; checks kept cheap; guidance fails open, blocks fail closed; hook output is a typed contract validated against the runtime's actual schema at build time; every soft payload ships firing telemetry + a yield query on a measured leash with a written pull condition.
card.guarantee: The firing is guaranteed by the runtime — impossible to forget. Boundary: a guidance payload aims deterministically but does not compel; only the blocking variant compels; a buggy hook's blast radius is the whole loop.
card.semantic_level: runtime lifecycle event → guaranteed check at that moment — deterministic delivery of policy at the decision point ('hard delivery of soft guidance').
card.forces_tradeoffs: Fires on every event occurrence, needed or not — must stay cheap or gets disabled. Nag/tune-out risk on misread state. The wired-but-dead failure (output shape silently dropped by the runtime) is the worst fail-open. Soft payloads are unmanageable without their own telemetry.
card.dependencies: A runtime exposing lifecycle events + registration; the measured-leash telemetry discipline; semantic-level-enforcement picks this rung for operator-loop properties; generalizes into reflection-facet-substrate at the second reflection hook.
card.known_uses: DocAble's turn-stop non-stop hook; the pre-compaction hand-off hook; the session-start alert-backlog ritual; the before-a-tool-call worktree guard; the build-time hook-output conformance check; the self-check hook whose telemetry closed the loop on its own yield.
card.likely_parent_family: Point-of-action policy delivery (runtime-event interposition)

card.failure_class: At the second policy-reflection nudge, N independent hooks destroy themselves: alarm fatigue kills the whole family together, each hook re-implements tempo/silence/telemetry machinery that drifts, and policy baked into payload strings rots when the canonical doc moves.
card.engineering_obligation: Aggregate soft policy nudges under one shared attention budget with uniform machinery and policy held by reference — cap the family's aggregate emission, not each member's.
card.solution_structure: A Template-Method facet base with a closed specialization surface (lint-enforced); a typed facet registry; a shared emitter bound to the lifecycle event that round-robins facets and emits at most one reflection per window; each facet declares a resolvable pointer into canonical policy material (pointer-resolve lint); follow-ups drawn from a closed vocabulary; per-firing telemetry + yield query (the measured leash).
card.guarantee: The aggregate nudge rate is mechanically capped (≤1/window) and facet uniformity holds by construction; every policy pointer resolves. Boundary: the reflections themselves are soft — default-silent, never blocking; no facet is guaranteed to fire on every eligible event.
card.semantic_level: policy dimension → paced operator reflection — an attention budget over a family of soft signals, with policy referenced (single-source) rather than copied.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Facets compete for the window: per-facet promptness traded for aggregate calm. The closed surface makes the base a coordination point for new capabilities. Pure over-engineering at N=1 — earns its keep at the second facet.
card.dependencies: lifecycle-hooks as the single-hook primitive; a canonical, referenceable policy corpus with a ref grammar; the measured-leash telemetry; meta-model-consumption (reference, don't copy).
card.known_uses: DocAble's ReflectionFacet base + typed registry with four facets (failure→mechanism, knowledge-routing, structural-drift, operations); the turn-end round-robin emitter; the closed-surface and pointer-resolve lints; the portable stdlib copy-and-adapt library shipped with the catalogue's skill.
card.likely_parent_family: Point-of-action policy delivery (feed-back aggregation over a shared tempo budget)

card.failure_class: The reclaim dilemma: without a durable close record, cleanup either deletes eagerly and destroys unlanded work or never deletes and leaks worktrees — 'done' is ambiguous between cherry-picked and deliberately abandoned; recurs at every agent completion.
card.engineering_obligation: An irreversible reclaim must be justified by a durable, machine-checkable close record carrying an explicit disposition — cleanup proves safety from the record instead of guessing intent off a branch.
card.solution_structure: A tombstone commit written at the worktree branch tip carrying a disposition from a small vocabulary (cherry-picked / declared-skipped); concurrent closers deduplicated via a registry event; a live-worktree guard refuses tombstoning any agent with a live marker; mass operations require explicit id-lists (runtime enumeration banned); cleanup verifies the predicate 'tombstone at tip AND every non-tombstone commit picked-or-skipped'.
card.guarantee: Cleanup can prove a worktree is reclaimable before removing it. Boundary: the reclaim trusts the record's correctness — a disposition that mis-records 'skipped' for unlanded work greenlights an unsafe reclaim.
card.semantic_level: lifecycle close → disposition record — the destructive operation ⊨ recorded proof that all work is accounted for.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The tombstone: bypass prefix skips the commit gate by design (honesty-dependent). Dedup depends on the registry event. Manual id-lists are deliberate friction against runtime enumeration.
card.dependencies: agent-registry (live markers + the dedup event); the commit substrate as the record store; cleanup-stale as the verifying consumer.
card.known_uses: DocAble's tombstone_commit.py disposition records; the tombstoning_started dedup event (exit 78); the cleanup-stale safe-to-reclaim predicate; the --id-file mass-tombstone discipline.
card.likely_parent_family: Authoritative lifecycle state (disposition-bearing close record)

card.failure_class: Silent substrate degradation under an un-reacting orchestrator: fleet health (cron, merge-train, tombstones) is invisible without a signal surface, so breakage accretes for hours while each dispatch still looks locally fine.
card.engineering_obligation: Make operational health a queryable, self-documenting, typo-proof signal surface, and bind every signal to a prescribed response — emission alone is not observability; the loop is emit → interpret → react.
card.solution_structure: A typed event bus whose topics form a closed const-string registry (lint-enforced, so a typo cannot create a dead topic); every topic carries a playbook entry (baseline-healthy · what-looks-wrong · response); a design-doc rule makes a topic without an observability block an incomplete design; the orchestrator polls on a defined cadence and reacts per playbook.
card.guarantee: Emission is mechanical and topics enumerable; the bus itself never blocks (the derived alerts gate does). Boundary: acting on the signal is orchestrator discipline — a perfect signal can still be ignored.
card.semantic_level: substrate event → typed topic → prescribed response — each signal carries its own interpretation and reaction, versus free-form logs that carry neither.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Only as useful as playbook coverage (the common gap). Consumption rests on poll cadence discipline. Every new topic is a registry row + emit wiring + playbook entry kept in sync.
card.dependencies: The const-string topic registry + its lint; operational-playbooks as the reaction half; cron-alerts-gate as the derived blocking consumer; sibling surfaces agent-registry and deploy-heartbeats.
card.known_uses: DocAble's event bus + topic registry; the event-bus playbook and the observability-block requirement on topic-introducing design docs; the session-start + post-cherry-pick monitoring cadence.
card.likely_parent_family: Fleet observability surfaces (typed signal with owned response)
card.abstract_name: Reactor loop over a typed signal surface

card.failure_class: An aggregate sweep job that internally fans out over the whole tree saturates the host on its own — two concurrent sweeps (or many agents each triggering one) melt the machine even though every individual invocation looks fine under per-call caps.
card.engineering_obligation: Treat an aggregate job as an indivisible admission unit: at most one whole-sweep in flight per host, and at most one being dispatched per orchestrator — a coarser instrument than per-invocation slots.
card.solution_structure: A whole-sweep singleton mutex (host flock at entry, hard-capped, fail-loud) plus an orchestrator-side in-flight declaration: every brief declares a compute-class and the orchestrator keeps only one aggregate-class brief in flight; a role gate refuses the sweep under the wrong role.
card.guarantee: At most one aggregate sweep per host mechanically; at most one in flight per orchestrator by declared accounting. Boundary: the in-flight half rests on honest compute-class declaration; bypass and under-declaration slip past.
card.semantic_level: sweep-as-unit → exclusive admission — the mediation relation applied at the granularity of the whole aggregate job, not its parts.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Serializes the heaviest gate into a throughput chokepoint under a busy fleet — deliberately. Half the mechanism is orchestrator discipline, not machinery. Mis-declared compute-class is the soft underbelly.
card.dependencies: Host mutex with hard timeout; compute-class declarations on briefs (via brief-linting); orchestrator in-flight accounting; the role gate from role-typed-dispatch.
card.known_uses: DocAble's lint-all host instance-lock (1800s cap); the compute-class brief declaration + one-in-flight rule; the role-enforcement gate refusing sonnet-active.
card.likely_parent_family: Mediated resource admission (whole-sweep singleton variant)

card.failure_class: Heavy parallel-safe tools (build, type-check, code query) from N worktrees oversubscribe one host's CPU/memory and slow everyone — but over-serializing them (N=1) would idle cores and stall the fleet; the failure is both oversubscription and over-serialization.
card.engineering_obligation: Ration parallel-safe-but-heavy shared compute at the host's capacity — choose the admission cardinality from the resource's contention profile (destructive ⇒ exclusive; parallel-safe-heavy ⇒ bounded M).
card.solution_structure: A host-level counting semaphore (byte-range flock, M=8 slots) that the identified set of heavy tools acquire before running; a per-tool enforcer on each routed tool refuses the unmediated call; per-run timestamped logs.
card.guarantee: At most M concurrent heavy-tool runs per host via the only available path. Boundary: coverage is only the routed tool set — an unrouted new heavy tool escapes the cap; M is a static guess.
card.semantic_level: every invocation → a bounded admission slot at the mediated seam — same mediation relation as the exclusive lock, at bounded cardinality.
card.forces_tradeoffs: M is fixed, not adaptive (too high melts a small host, too low wastes a big one). Each routed tool is an enforcer surface that can drift. Log proliferation. The cardinality choice itself is the design judgment.
card.dependencies: A counting-semaphore primitive; the enumerated adjacent-tool set; per-tool enforcers; sibling test-serializer (N=1) and the aggregate-compute mutex above it.
card.known_uses: DocAble's build-serializer.py M=8 byte-range semaphore over dotnet build / tsc / csharp-query / jedi lints / pyright, with five active enforcers.
card.likely_parent_family: Mediated resource admission (fixed-cardinality variant, bounded M)

card.failure_class: Cardinality caps bound how many heavy jobs run, not whether the host can bear them now: work gets dispatched into an already-saturated host and burns wall-clock polling at the mediators, and pressure that rises after admission leaves a too-heavy job running unchecked.
card.engineering_obligation: Admit and continue heavy work only under bearable live conditions — one shared pressure signal consulted at both moments work is admitted and executed, so the two layers cannot disagree.
card.solution_structure: A host monitor emitting a coarse pressure level (GREEN/YELLOW/RED) over the saturable resource, read by three consumers: a pre-dispatch admission gate that refuses/defers heavy briefs under RED; an execution-time shed at the compute mediators that stops heavy work pressure has overtaken; and a plain callable advisory read for operator judgment.
card.guarantee: Heavy work is neither started into nor left running on a RED host (where wired). Boundary: coarse thresholds are a tuning surface; light work must be classed out or it gets starved; as-built the load-pressure admission gate is a flagged extension (shed + disk-floor gate wired).
card.semantic_level: work admission/continuation ⊨ live resource condition — gating on the state of the environment, versus the cardinality mediators' gating on the count of admitted work.
card.forces_tradeoffs: GREEN/YELLOW/RED is blunt: too-eager starves throughput, too-lax admits overload. Refusal must be deferral-with-wake, never silent drop, or sustained RED starves the queue. Split-brain risk if admission and shed read different signals/thresholds. The advisory read cannot enforce.
card.dependencies: A cheap live pressure signal; a pre-dispatch gate seam beside existing admission checks (disk floor, quota); the compute mediators as the shed point; a heavy-vs-light work classification.
card.known_uses: DocAble's GREEN/YELLOW/RED host-load monitor read by the compute mediators for refuse-and-shed; the free-disk-floor pre-dispatch gate (the load-pressure admission sibling is the flagged as-built gap); the callable monitor for YELLOW-aware dispatch judgment.
card.likely_parent_family: Mediated resource admission — but the directive flags this family may SPLIT by forces/guarantees: fixed-capacity concurrency mediation vs adaptive pressure-based admission + shedding; this card is the adaptive pole.

card.failure_class: Concurrent test runs from multiple worktrees on one host contend destructively (ports, shared artifacts, I/O): tests flake or hang for reasons unrelated to the code, agents chase non-bugs, wall-clock blows up — recurs whenever two agents test at once, i.e. constantly under a fleet.
card.engineering_obligation: Mediate mutually destructive use of a shared resource down to a single writer, with the raw unmediated path structurally impossible rather than conventionally discouraged.
card.solution_structure: A host-level wrapper acquiring an exclusive flock (N=1) before invoking the tool, a fail-loud wait cap bounding a stuck lock, and — decisively — an in-assembly module-initializer enforcer that refuses the raw invocation from agent-worktree CWDs, making the mediated path the only path.
card.guarantee: At most one test run per host, and agents cannot take the raw path. Boundary: single-host only; the audited human bypass reintroduces contention if misused.
card.semantic_level: every invocation → the authorized mediated seam — resource access flows through a single-writer admission point (exclusive cardinality).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Serialization is deliberate wall-clock cost: a long run queues every other worktree. A stuck lock stalls everyone (bounded by the fail-loud cap). The bypass is a hole. Coordinates one machine only.
card.dependencies: A host-global lock file; an interception point inside the tool (module initializer) so the ban is structural; sibling build-serializer for the adjacent parallel-safe tools; the role/compute-class declarations upstream.
card.known_uses: DocAble's test-serializer.py N=1 flock on dotnet test (+ auto coverage collection on fuzz filters); TestMediatorEnforcer [ModuleInitializer]; the audited bypass env var.
card.likely_parent_family: Mediated resource admission (fixed-cardinality variant, N=1 exclusive)
card.abstract_name: Single-writer resource mediation with structural ban

models-bridge/system-models/agent-first-.title: Agent-first MBSE harness (frozen records; adopt schema, skip runtime)

card.failure_class: A modeling layer that either doesn't fit your invariants (a real tool's schema is fixed; project-specific derived fields don't map) or doesn't wire into your build (a solver checks the model against itself, never against the running code) — so the model drifts, and a drifted model is worse than none.
card.engineering_obligation: The modeling substrate must express the project's own invariants AND reconcile against the code inside the build — adopt the best genre's vocabulary and schema per view, hand-roll and own the executable layer.
card.solution_structure: A thin harness over plain frozen typed records with five recurring disciplines: (1) the look-up seam (model fields loaded/derived from the code at build, never hand-copied); (2) derive-don't-hand-type + a stored-equals-derived assertion lint; (3) an auto-discovery loader (no central manifest); (4) a per-view drift-lint contract (load model, load code, set-diff, re-run derivations, exit non-zero); (5) a generic record→JSON query projection. Shared harness packaged; per-view drift lints deliberately hand-rolled.
card.guarantee: Per view, the model is unable to lie about the code (the drift lint is the counted sensor). Boundary: degrades to a snapshot the moment a view stops following the look-up/derive/drift disciplines.
card.semantic_level: model field → projection of code (derivation reconciled at build time), plus model vocabulary ⟷ genre standard (schema adopted, runtime skipped — portability preserved).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Five disciplines to actually hold per view. A drift lint per view is real, deliberately-unshared surface. Deciding what to model and in which genre's vocabulary is design work — model only where a failure lives.
card.dependencies: executable-source-of-truth (this is its construction method); drift-parity-gates (discipline 4 IS those gates); model-driven-codegen and query-surface downstream; the genre vocabularies (SysML, Backstage, TLA+, C4) as adoptable schemas.
card.known_uses: DocAble's system-models directory of frozen dataclasses with auto-discovery loader and generic JSON projection; the derived verification-tier field with its stored-equals-derived lint; the Backstage-dialect service-flow view; the portable 4+1-view starter-kit scaffolds shipped with the catalogue's skill.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable source of truth (construction-method variant: the harness)

card.failure_class: The fleet that builds the product goes unmodeled: its lifecycle and the orchestrator's own loop live implicitly across dispatch/registry/tombstone/worktree tools — an agent reaches a state no transition allows, the orchestrator rests with ratified work queued, fleet invariants (exactly-one-live-marker, upload-before-teardown) are asserted nowhere, and the reflection substrate drifts from anything modeled.
card.engineering_obligation: Model the production substrate with the same method pointed at the product — the fleet becomes as checkable as the software it builds (the developer-journey subject of the same MBSE method).
card.solution_structure: Two typed state machines (the agent lifecycle dispatch→…→tombstone→clean with the abandoned/recovered branch; the orchestrator's observe→land+DoD→refill→bank→rest loop); a closed typed seam set (hooks, registry, mediator pressure signal, status files, event bus, facet registry); fleet invariants with verification tiers DERIVED from temporal shape; the reflection-facet registry as first-class modeled nodes reconciled both ways against the live registry; the same drift/parity rails, audit-only → blocking.
card.guarantee: Model = territory over the fleet substrate; hairy concurrency invariants are forced onto exhaustive checkers by derivation, not judgment. Boundary: inherits the product method's ceremony — worth it because the fleet runs hourly and its failures are expensive.
card.semantic_level: fleet lifecycle + operator loop legality — the developer-journey behavioral relation; the trunk method reified toward the orchestration subject.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Modeling the operator's own loop feels like navel-gazing until it catches a real dynamics-only failure (resting with work queued; a facet silently off-registry).
card.dependencies: The trunk method reused wholesale (tier derivation, coordination/temporal types, drift machinery); the agent-registry and reflection-facet substrates as the reconciliation anchors; siblings service-flow/user-journey (same method, product subject).
card.known_uses: DocAble's agent_orch model: the two machines, the closed seam set, derived-tier fleet invariants, and the facet nodes with two-way registry reconciliation.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — fleet/orchestration lifecycle (the method's second subject arm)

card.failure_class: 'Which component owns this file, what zone, what boundaries and seams' answered ad hoc — a hardcoded path list here, a grep there — drifting the moment a directory moves, each tool passing while reasoning about a stale map; and agents lack the map that tells them where they are.
card.engineering_obligation: Code ownership, zones, boundary kinds, and sanctioned seams are named once in a typed registry every consumer queries, held equal to the real tree by bidirectional parity.
card.solution_structure: A typed component registry (leaf/group/meta kinds, focus-dirs, tags, docs, manifests) plus boundary/seam/read-surface classifiers; a reverse-mapping test asserting model ↔ tree parity in both directions; consumers (lint fleet, dispatch, context injection, the severity grader) read it rather than inferring from layout.
card.guarantee: A moved directory fails the parity test instead of silently staling each tool's private inference; every tool reads the same answer. Boundary: centralization blast radius — a wrong zone misroutes every consumer at once (the cost of the fix-once affordance).
card.semantic_level: file → owning component / zone / boundary — the structural ownership relation.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Add-a-component upkeep (registry row + boundary classification or the test fails, deliberately). The zone's meaning (boundary kind, seams) is not in the layout at all — only a model can carry it.
card.dependencies: drift-parity-gates (the reverse-mapping test); consumers: dynamic-context-injection, role-typed-dispatch, model-graded-finding-severity, the lint fleet; meta-model-consumption + query-surface as read paths.
card.known_uses: DocAble's component registry read by the lint fleet, dispatch, and audit surfaces; the boundary/seam classifiers; the reverse-mapping parity test.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — structural ownership map

models-bridge/system-models/composed-sta.title: Composed state-machine model (typed lifecycles + cross-machine invariants)

card.failure_class: The correctness properties of a distributed lifecycle span its machines but are asserted nowhere: scattered status flags mutated from many call sites; a rare interleaving double-completes a job, a crash strands a corrupt output as 'done', a requeue races a terminal write — per-machine tests green while the composition is broken.
card.engineering_obligation: The concurrency composition is one authored, checkable object: which machines exist, how they compose, and the predicates that must hold ACROSS them — each predicate carrying a derived verification obligation.
card.solution_structure: Each lifecycle a typed machine (state enum, transition table naming every legal edge, terminal-safe set — illegal transitions unrepresentable); the machines declared as a composed set with their hand-off seams; cross-machine invariants as first-class entities each with a required temporal form that routes it to its checker (safety → exhaustive state-space, liveness → temporal checker, linear → property test); a drift gate reconciles declared states against the live lifecycle vocabulary.
card.guarantee: Legality is structural and the composition's predicates are proven within the modeled bounds — the specification the verifier runs against. Boundary: exhaustive only over the modeled interleavings; proof as strong as the model's fidelity.
card.semantic_level: composed lifecycle legality + cross-machine predicates — what may happen over time, across machines (distinct from any single machine's graph).
card.forces_tradeoffs: The value and the cost both concentrate in naming the cross-machine predicates — the part a single-machine view never forces. A new state or invariant is a model edit or the gate fails.
card.dependencies: formal-invariant-verification (the proof engine this is the specification for); process-view (the other projection of the same concurrency); concurrency-contracts one layer beneath; executable-source-of-truth substrate.
card.known_uses: DocAble's parent-job / per-chunk / fan-in completer machines declared together; a dozen-plus cross-service invariants (lease-or-free exclusivity, upload-before-terminal-write, exactly-one-completer, preemption re-entry order) each carrying a temporal form.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — composed lifecycle machines (the specification side of formal verification)

card.failure_class: Undeclared mediation and single-writer contracts: an enforcer only sees the calls that reach it, so a newly-added subprocess or state mutator is simply not covered — a raw invocation slips the serializer, a second writer corrupts state, and the breakage is a race discovered late.
card.engineering_obligation: 'Who may run this, and how many at once' is declared as data, so COVERAGE can be checked against the code — the contract set complete, not just enforced at the seams that happen to be wired.
card.solution_structure: Two typed registries: a mediator registry (subprocess → serializer, cap, bypass-env) and a single-writer registry (state-mutation function → monopoly contract); enforcers keyed on the registries refuse unmediated calls; coverage lints flag a mediated-class call or a mutator that isn't contracted.
card.guarantee: An uncovered subprocess or mutator is a named finding rather than a latent race. Boundary: a declared-but-unenforced contract is documentation — the guarantee needs both the registry and the enforcer.
card.semantic_level: invocation/mutation → declared concurrency contract — the coverage relation over the mediation regime.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A registry entry per new mediated subprocess or contracted mutator. The contract is only as good as its enforcer.
card.dependencies: The agent mediators-and-resource-locks family (the enforcement half); synchronization-model (the OS-lock layer beneath); drift-parity-gates (the coverage lints).
card.known_uses: DocAble's mediator registry (test/build serializers, the lint mutex, the commit-slave serializer) and single-writer registry with their enforcers and coverage lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — concurrency contracts (the declaration side of mediated resource admission)

card.failure_class: A control portfolio that grows toward the last painful failure: effort piles onto the target that just hurt while another governance target accretes nothing, and the imbalance stays invisible — no artifact ever asks whether the control SET is balanced — until the unwatched target fails in a way a control would have caught.
card.engineering_obligation: Audit the governance estate itself against a closed taxonomy of complementary control targets carrying a completeness claim — re-derived from the live control set on every query, never a hand-kept audit that rots.
card.solution_structure: Each control's governance target is derived from its own code anchor by a rule (fail-loud on any control it cannot place — no silent default bucket); a read-only projection rolls the control node-set up per target with its soft/hard enforcement shape; an empty or all-soft target is a first-class finding naming the estate's blind spot; instrument-only — it aims the next control, never gates a commit.
card.guarantee: The classification cannot silently mis-credit (the fail-loud classifier is the hard half); the coverage map re-derives on every query so gaps open and close automatically. Boundary: measures balance, not quality — a populated target counts covered even if its controls are weak.
card.semantic_level: control → governance target — portfolio completeness over a closed complementary-targets taxonomy; reflexive (the control set audits itself).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Honest partial coverage is the feature — a stated zero drives the next work. A target the taxonomy can't express forces a taxonomy change (the doctrine grew a dimension). Balance ≠ strength.
card.dependencies: governance-graph (supplies the typed control node-set this rolls up); the closed targets taxonomy; stable per-control anchors; counterpart reflection-facet-substrate (the reactive supply whose failure-driven bias this proactive audit corrects).
card.known_uses: DocAble's control-target axis over the agent/models-bridge/product node-set; the roll-up that read one target populated and two at zero, driving a fix-wave from zero to a dozen controls; the census's own anchor-drift guard (it censuses its own governor).
card.likely_parent_family: Governance-of-governance (the coverage view of the control machinery)

card.failure_class: Substrate assumptions buried in control bodies: a substrate migration then misfires the fleet two silent ways at once — false FAILs (controls validating manifests that no longer exist, deploy-blocking on a no-baseline gate) and false PASSes (migrated services vanishing from every totality check) — and the blast radius is knowable only by grep-plus-read-every-body.
card.engineering_obligation: Every control declares the substrate assumption it bakes in as a typed fact, so 'what breaks when I change this substrate' is a computed query before the change, not an archaeology after it.
card.solution_structure: A closed stance enum added to each control's existing metadata block (assumes-plane-A-only / plane-B-only / branches-per-plane / agnostic); a query joins the declarations against the substrate model and emits the blast-radius table per target substrate; a declaration lint requires the stance on every substrate-reading control (audit-only → blocking); the deploy realization gate refuses to ship undeclared consumers.
card.guarantee: The migration blast radius is computed from declarations, not hand-maintained or grepped. Boundary: only as expressive as the stance enum — a stance it can't express forces an enum change (the honest signal the substrate grew a dimension).
card.semantic_level: control → substrate assumption — the governance fleet's own dependency edges made typed and queryable (the control machinery becomes a modeled element).
card.forces_tradeoffs: One declaration per substrate-reading control (the intended tax). Pays off only at a substrate change — a design-time-on-the-predictive-smell control, over-built if added to a substrate you'll never change.
card.dependencies: deployment-topology-model (the substrate model joined against); the existing control-metadata convention (adopt the schema you already lint); query-surface; extends meta-model-consumption from values to dependency edges.
card.known_uses: DocAble's typed plane-assumption on every topology-reading lint; the plane-deps query printing which lints a GKE↔Cloud-Run migration puts in scope; the declaration lint + deploy-gate fold-in.
card.likely_parent_family: Governance-of-governance (modeling the control machinery; typed-edge kin of invariant-dag-execution-policy)

models-bridge/system-models/coverage-mod.title: Coverage → model-node mapping (which invariants are tested)

card.failure_class: False test adequacy: 90% line coverage while a critical race invariant has zero tests touching its states — coverage counts lines, not meanings, so the invariants that matter most hide inside a high aggregate number.
card.engineering_obligation: Measure test adequacy against the system's meanings — per model node (state, seam, invariant), 'is this tested?' must be a queried fact, not a guess from a percentage.
card.solution_structure: A mapping that projects the suite's coverage data onto the structured model's nodes (via a node→code join at function granularity), yielding a per-node fact: covered / uncovered / by-which-tests; used first as a backlog (the model becomes the test work-list), promotable to a gate for critical nodes.
card.guarantee: Per-node coverage is a queryable fact that a threshold cannot hide. Boundary: a covered node is exercised, not proven (pair with formal verification); sharpness limited by coverage granularity and the fidelity of the node→code join.
card.semantic_level: test coverage → model node — the exercise relation over meanings rather than lines.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The node→code join is load-bearing (mis-mapped nodes get mis-attributed coverage). Function granularity can't split two invariants in one function. Gating everything starves throughput; gating nothing leaves criticals untested — criticality scoping is the tuning surface.
card.dependencies: Structured model with addressable nodes (executable-source-of-truth); attributable coverage data; a criticality policy; counterpart formal-invariant-verification (proof vs exercise).
card.known_uses: DocAble's coverage-reference mapping onto the cross-service state-machine model's nodes at function granularity; the uncovered-critical-nodes sweep as work-list.
card.likely_parent_family: Model-derived assurance coverage

models-bridge/system-models/data-flow-mo.title: Compliance data-flow model (typed sinks & edges for privacy)

card.failure_class: Privacy and erasure answered by memory and grep: the erasure runs, reports success, and leaves data in the cache, log stream, or third-party sink nobody remembered — and information-flow violations are unenumerable because no one listed the sinks or the edges between them.
card.engineering_obligation: Where a governed data kind can flow is a typed graph — sinks and transfer edges, typed by category — over which compliance properties are evaluated as walks, including the transitive question no flat list can answer.
card.solution_structure: Typed sink nodes (tables, caches, blob stores, log streams, vendors) and transfer edges, typed by data category; a policy evaluator walks the graph for erasability ('every personal-data sink has a covering erasure path'), permitted-flow, and retention; the graph reconciled against the real write and transfer sites so an unmodeled store is a build finding.
card.guarantee: A new sink or transfer without model coverage reddens the gate; policy questions are model walks. Boundary: the evaluator is confidently wrong wherever the graph diverges — reconciliation is what earns trust.
card.semantic_level: data category → transitively-reachable sinks — the governed flow relation with obligations (erasure, permitted-flow) attached.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Edges — especially third-party transfers — are where the real graph hides and where maintenance concentrates. Earns its cost only for a data kind carrying a real obligation.
card.dependencies: A policy evaluator; drift-parity-gates (site reconciliation); formal-invariant-verification (flow predicates provable over the declared graph); deployment-topology-model (physical placement of the named sinks).
card.known_uses: DocAble's typed sink-and-edge registry over personal-data flows, with erasure and information-flow policies evaluated over it.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — governed data-flow graph

card.failure_class: Deployment facts hardcoded in deploy scripts and import checks drift from the real topology: a service moves tier, a layer boundary is quietly crossed, and the deploy or an architectural invariant breaks — with no check until the break.
card.engineering_obligation: Where things run and how they layer is declared once — topology, tier classes, layer boundaries — and parity-checked against the real deploy tables and import graph.
card.solution_structure: A typed topology loader for the managed deployment, a service-tier registry, and layer-boundary contracts for the agent substrate; deploy scripts and layering lints read them; a deploy-phase-table parity lint and import-layer boundary checks gate on divergence.
card.guarantee: A moved tier or crossed boundary fails a lint at author time. Boundary: declared boundaries block expedient cross-layer imports — a real, deliberate cost.
card.semantic_level: service → tier / layer / host placement — the physical-topology relation plus layering constraints.
