card.forces_tradeoffs: Topology changes are model edits (or parity failures). Layering contracts constrain the code on purpose.
card.dependencies: model-driven-codegen (deploy/env generation); consumers control-substrate-dependency (the substrate joined against) and invariant-dag-execution-policy (the host taxonomy); drift-parity-gates.
card.known_uses: DocAble's deployment-topology loader, service-tier registry, and layer-boundary contracts; the deploy-phase-table parity and import-layer lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — physical deployment topology

card.failure_class: Domain facts restated in code, docs, and dashboards drift: the supported-filetype list diverges across five sites, a rule's metadata goes stale, the competitor doc is out of date — small correctness and stale-doc failures multiplied across many slices.
card.engineering_obligation: Each domain fact has exactly one typed home that tools read and docs are generated from — the fact canonicalized per slice, coverage/parity-linted.
card.solution_structure: A set of small frozen typed registries (supported filetypes, WCAG coverage gaps, periodic-GC cron entries, UX write-authority, competitor set, rule metadata), each with consumers that read it, generators that emit its doc surfaces, and a coverage/parity lint plus a doc-derived pin.
card.guarantee: A consumer that diverges fails the build; frozen sets make expedient edits deliberate model changes. Boundary: breadth, not depth — each registry is simple but each is a surface.
card.semantic_level: domain fact → single typed source — fact canonicalization, one home per slice.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Many small registries to maintain. Frozen-set friction is deliberate.
card.dependencies: drift-parity-gates per registry; the rule-metadata registry feeds claude-md-rule-index; the WCAG-gap registry feeds the standards rule engine; model-driven-codegen for the doc generation.
card.known_uses: DocAble's supported-filetypes, WCAG-gap, periodic-GC-cron, UX-write-authority, competitor, and rule-metadata registries with their generators and lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — domain-fact registries

card.failure_class: Silent model drift: the model says one thing, the code does another, and everything downstream (dispatch, codegen, deploy) reasons from a lie — worse than absence because the model looks authoritative; recurs whenever either side changes without the other.
card.engineering_obligation: Keep the map equal to the territory bidirectionally — neither the model nor the reality may drift unilaterally; one-way regeneration cannot express a model that also generates parts of the code.
card.solution_structure: A family of parity checks, one (or a pair) per model, each reading the model at lint time and comparing against machine-readable reality in both directions (every model row ↔ a real thing on disk AND every real thing ↔ a model row), blocking the build on divergence.
card.guarantee: Divergence in either direction fails the build. Boundary: only for the modeled relations, and only as good as the parity predicate — a wrong predicate yields false drift or false confidence.
card.semantic_level: model ⟷ reality — bidirectional parity as a build-blocking invariant.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A gate per model to author and maintain (real enforcement breadth). Bidirectionality is stricter — it fails on legitimate transitions, which is the point (both sides must move together).
card.dependencies: A machine-readable model and reality to compare; blocking gate placement; the executable-source-of-truth substrate; generalized by symbol-anchored-traceability-graph; product-side sibling coherence-lints.
card.known_uses: DocAble's service-flow parity lint (tree↔yaml both ways), public-API drift lint (handler↔spec), service-call-graph drift lint, deploy-phase-table parity, k8s parity lints, sync-coverage lint, model↔tree reverse-mapping tests.
card.likely_parent_family: Drift/parity gate (canonical pattern)

card.failure_class: No shared, authoritative, compact representation of the system: the codebase exceeds any agent's context window, so agents (and humans) re-derive the architecture badly and drift; prose architecture docs go stale because nothing forces them true.
card.engineering_obligation: Maintain authoritative system knowledge as machine-readable typed data that is continuously consumed and mechanically held true — the interface through which a context-bounded actor operates a context-exceeding system.
card.solution_structure: A catalog of structured models (typed data importing nothing) that tools, lints, and deploy scripts read on every run and generate real artifacts from; every model is pinned by a characterization test, held true by a drift/parity gate, and constantly exercised; consumption preference: a stable lint that reads the meta-file > codegen > a hand-rolled copy.
card.guarantee: The build fails the moment a model diverges from the code (via the gates), so drift surfaces as a failed build, not a stale paragraph. Boundary: 'cannot drift' holds only while every model has a gate and stays continuously consumed.
card.semantic_level: model ⟷ reality — the map held equal to the territory, with the model also authoritative source generating parts of the territory.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Real upkeep tedium — exactly what stopped humans doing MBSE, and what agents dissolve. An authoritative-looking wrong model is worse than none (hence gates are not optional). What to model, and in which dialect, is up-front design work.
card.dependencies: drift-parity-gates (the counterpart that makes 'cannot drift' true); agent-first-mbse-harness (the construction method); model-driven-codegen, query-surface, meta-model-consumption (the faces); every is-a-model entry rides on it.
card.known_uses: DocAble's model catalog (~60 typed models; Backstage-dialect YAML for services, typed loaders for the rest); per-model doc-derived characterization pins; the lint-reads-meta-file preference order.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable source of truth (canonical pattern — the bridge flagship)

models-bridge/system-models/formal-invar.title: Formal invariant verification (temporal form → model check)

card.failure_class: Invariants believed true while a rare interleaving violates them: sampled tests miss the one adversarial schedule; the same invariant restated in prose/assertion/spec drifts apart; and a mis-declared liveness property routed to a safety checker is structurally blind to its violation, with zero signal.
card.engineering_obligation: Verify each invariant by the method its property class demands — the temporal shape (safety vs liveness) is a required, consumed routing input that derives the checker, never a decorative annotation.
card.solution_structure: A required temporal-form field on every model invariant ([]P / []<>P / P ~> Q); a derivation routes the invariant from its operator to the checker its shape demands (exhaustive state-space BFS for safety, a temporal model checker for liveness); a match lint asserts the routed checker fits the operator, making mis-routing a build error; reuse one mature formal engine rather than building parallel ones.
card.guarantee: A routed invariant is proven across every interleaving of the bounded modeled state space, or yields a concrete counterexample trace. Boundary: exhaustive only within bounds and only as faithful as the model's abstraction of the real system.
card.semantic_level: invariant's temporal shape → verification method — the property class ⊨ prover strength relation (safety/liveness made explicit and consumed).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Heavier than unit tests — dev/CI cadence, not per-commit; the derived tier keeps cheap invariants on cheap checkers. A decorative unconsumed temporal string is worse than none: it looks verified and isn't (the match lint exists for this).
card.dependencies: A structured invariant model (executable-source-of-truth); at least one exhaustive checker; the shape↔checker match lint; sibling journey-criticality-test-placement (same derive-a-tier-from-a-typed-trait move).
card.known_uses: DocAble's temporal operators on the cross-service state model; the TLA+-family checker plus the bounded-BFS 'simworld'; the match lint; the state model named in SysML vocabulary (adopt the schema, skip the runtime).
card.likely_parent_family: Model-derived assurance coverage (trait-derived verification routing)

card.failure_class: Two guardrails placing contradictory or contending demands on one shared resource — a commit-set required to be squashed by one path and scope-checked by another, two turn-end hooks with no declared order each able to block — invisible in any single mechanism's code, found only when a real operation trips both; grows pairwise with every mechanism added.
card.engineering_obligation: Model the control system itself: the interactions between governance mechanisms as typed conflict edges over a closed shared-resource vocabulary, so a proposed mechanism's collisions are checkable at authoring, not at the tripwire.
card.solution_structure: Mechanism nodes typed by firing event, reads/writes/locks over a closed resource vocabulary (the turn-end slot and context budget are resources too), output power, and soft/hard; conflict edges in a closed four-value taxonomy (contradiction / contention / ordering / soft-vs-hard) each naming the resource and a resolution; each edge's deterministic-vs-judgment nature DERIVED from its conflict type (decidable edges route to a sensor, semantic ones to a human prompt); a check-new query runs the deterministic checks against a spec before wiring; a drift lint re-resolves node anchors against the wired reality.
card.guarantee: Mechanically-decidable conflict classes (same-slot no-order, lock cycles) are caught by construction; judgment edges are surfaced, not decided. Boundary: a stale interaction graph is worse than none — the drift lint is mandatory; resource granularity is a real tuning surface.
card.semantic_level: control × control → conflict over a shared resource — the interaction dual of the control census; the join key is the typed resource, not the call.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Too-coarse resources drown real conflicts in false edges; too-fine is noise. The model describes rather than mandates — governance of governance risks the tower nobody wants, so it hardens only where a collision recurs.
card.dependencies: synchronization-model (the ordering/deadlock analysis generalized beyond OS locks); the agent-family mechanisms as its nodes; symbol-anchored derivation discipline for the node↔code join; query-surface; control-coverage-census as the sibling coverage view of the same node-set.
card.known_uses: DocAble's governance-graph model with the two canonical collision edges (the commit-set contradiction, the turn-end contention); the check-new pre-wiring consistency query; the anchor drift lint.
card.likely_parent_family: Governance-of-governance (the interaction view — the canonical Governance Graph pattern)

models-bridge/system-models/invariant-da.title: Invariant-DAG execution policy (typed Scheduler: correctness vs resource + cost)

card.failure_class: A dependency graph that lies to its reader: resource rationing and cost gates spelled in the same needs= syntax as correctness edges, per-environment conditionals mutating the graph per host — so removing a stale wait takes multi-paragraph archaeology, a rationing edge ships to an elastic host, and an over-broad strip silently disables a real gate.
card.engineering_obligation: Keep the correctness statement host-invariant and make every edge declare why it exists; environment-specific execution concerns (concurrency, budget) are a typed policy layer over the graph, never mutations of it.
card.solution_structure: A closed edge-intent enum (CORRECTNESS / COST_GATE / LOAD): only the first two live in the graph, identical across hosts over the shared roster; LOAD migrates out to a typed Scheduler mapping a per-host (concurrency-ceiling, budget) profile to a ConcurrencyPlan of semaphores + per-COST_GATE honor decisions, emitting per-wave rationing records; two lints hold the separation (no LOAD edge in the graph, read from the Scheduler's own permitted-intent set; cross-host edge-set consistency).
card.guarantee: The graph never changes shape per host; raising a ceiling or moving a stress test is a profile-row edit, never graph code. Boundary: the edge→semaphore migration is behavior-identical only at N=1 — the low-concurrency host needs a pinned serialization check or a silent concurrency regression ships.
card.semantic_level: dependency edge → declared intent — correctness vs economy vs contention as typed edge semantics; execution plan ⊨ host profile.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Every edge gains an intent annotation (the price of legibility). Two rationing layers may coexist (deploy Scheduler vs host mediators) until unified. The cross-host graph diff is expensive — deploy-scope, not per-commit.
card.dependencies: deployment-topology-model (the host taxonomy the profile keys on); a step selector/roster; executable-source-of-truth + drift gates; sibling control-substrate-dependency (same typed-edge-metadata reflex on a different graph).
card.known_uses: DocAble's EdgeIntent enum + frozen DAG_RESIDENT_INTENTS set on the deploy driver; the Scheduler with three host profiles (local permits-1, staging unbounded, production low-finite); the load-edge and host-superset lints (audit-only, zero findings by construction).
card.likely_parent_family: Typed-edge semantics over modeled graphs (with control-substrate-dependency); secondarily a policy layer of the executable-source-of-truth family

models-bridge/system-models/journey-crit.title: Journey-criticality → test-tier placement (which host a test runs on)

card.failure_class: The local-green/staging-red surprise: which test runs in which environment tier is a hand-drawn line that drifts, so a major user path ends up staging-only — the fast local gate passes and is trusted to mean more than it covers, and the broken revenue-core flow surfaces late.
card.engineering_obligation: Derive verification placement from a typed importance trait — the tier is a pure function of criticality, stored nowhere by hand — and hold a floor guaranteeing the cheap gate covers everything designated major.
card.solution_structure: A typed criticality axis on journey parts; a total derivation criticality→tier computed at model load (moving a part off the fast tier requires a visible criticality reclassification, never a silent tier edit); a coverage-floor lint (every major part maps to a real test in a sanctioned local home); a per-context selector — a pure function from deploy context to the concrete test roster — that the deploy driver gates each phase on; host containment is a semilattice checked by property test + a live-model lint.
card.guarantee: Local-green ⟹ every major path ran locally, as a checked property. Boundary: the floor closes absence, not quality — a hollow stub passes; that residual stays human (picked up by journey-task-closure).
card.semantic_level: journey criticality → verification host tier — an importance trait deriving placement, plus a checked containment ordering over hosts.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A join-key annotation cost on every journey. Reclassification friction is deliberate (over-marking major grows the local tier). A two-value cut may mis-fit larger products — extend the derivation, don't hand-place outliers.
card.dependencies: user-journey-model (the carrier) and service-flow-model (the typed journey entities); executable-source-of-truth + drift gates; siblings formal-invariant-verification and journey-task-closure (the derive-from-a-trait family).
card.known_uses: DocAble's MAJOR/MINOR journey-part derivation to local-depth vs staging-full; the coverage-floor lint (landed audit-only over a known gap); the per-context selector imported by the cluster-deploy driver in place of per-environment conditionals.
card.likely_parent_family: Model-derived assurance coverage (trait-derived test placement)

models-bridge/system-models/journey-task.title: Journey task-closure (typed terminal post-condition → derived strength)

card.failure_class: The flow-vs-task gap: a journey test greens on 'the URL loaded' while the artifact the user came for never paints — the terminal assertion sits one hop short of the goal, and 'what done means' lives in prose no check can compare against the spec's real assertion.
card.engineering_obligation: The meaning of a journey's terminal assertion is typed data whose strength is derivable and gated — a major journey's test may not assert less than task closure.
card.solution_structure: A typed closure block on the journey entity: a sealed boolean algebra (AND/OR/NOT, deliberately non-temporal) over a reviewed library of leaf predicates preferring accessibility observables; flow-only leaves (navigated, 2xx) exist but cannot constitute a closure alone; a pure total derivation yields TASK_CLOSED / FLOW_ONLY / DISABLED; a gate makes a major journey deriving FLOW_ONLY a finding; forward-policing lints; audit-only-first landing while the backlog drains.
card.guarantee: A major journey's terminal assertion provably has the shape of task closure, and the same typed closure resolves through a second resolver (a headless canary probe) pre-promotion. Boundary: closes meaning, not robustness — deep-vs-shallow assertion stays human review.
card.semantic_level: terminal assertion ⊨ task outcome — the test's meaning held equal to the user's goal, with strength derived from the expression's shape.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The leaf library must extend by reviewed registry addition or it sprawls into bespoke predicates. A disabled closure must stay visible as DISABLED, not vanish into green. Audit-only-first is the honest landing for unmigrated journeys.
card.dependencies: user-journey-model (the carrier); the criticality axis to scope the gate; observable resolvers (a11y roles, HTTP status, file magic); drift-parity thinking applied to the terminal assertion; sibling journey-criticality-test-placement (picks up where its floor stops).
card.known_uses: DocAble's typed closure blocks on major journeys ('artifact rendered AND content inspectable AND no error-fallback' — the fixed form of a real one-hop-past production break); the strength gate; the canary closure-probe closing the configuration-only-break containment hole.
card.likely_parent_family: Model-derived assurance coverage (typed post-condition with derived strength)

models-bridge/system-models/lifecycle-mo.title: Lifecycle model (typed operational map → generated runbook)

card.failure_class: Operating knowledge living in one head plus stale docs: the operator diagnoses from memory (wrong precisely on the rare failure that matters), a memory-less agent re-derives the substrate from cold every time, and the runbook that would have helped rots silently because nothing ties the prose to the system.
card.engineering_obligation: How the substrate works is a typed map — each operating lifecycle carries a machine-checkable healthy-state predicate, each symptom keys to its lifecycle, and the operator's runbook is GENERATED from the map so it cannot drift from the system it describes.
card.solution_structure: Named lifecycle nodes (dispatch-and-reclaim, context banking, repo deployability, the deploy staircase, dev-env, the periodic plane, the orchestrator's hooks), each with a one-line mechanics summary and an executable healthy predicate; symptom→fix rows keyed to lifecycles; the runbook/skill projected from the model; the flat perimeter of small mechanisms grouped under the lifecycles they serve.
card.guarantee: The runbook is a projection of the same map the health checks read — prose cannot disagree with the model. Boundary: a drifted healthy predicate gives false confidence; the generation gate surfaces out-of-date maps.
card.semantic_level: operational subsystem → healthy-state predicate + symptom keying — the operations relation, with prose as a projection of the model.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Models the operator's own work (navel-gazing until a fresh agent resolves an incident in seconds from a generated runbook keyed to a failing health check). Predicates must stay honest.
card.dependencies: model-driven-codegen (the generation move applied to operator docs); operator-runbook-skill (the projected artifact); sibling agent-orchestration-model (transitions vs operations of the same substrate).
card.known_uses: DocAble's typed operating map of the fleet substrate with per-lifecycle healthy predicates; the lifecycle-keyed symptom catalog; the generated operator skill (positive map first, troubleshooting as keyed fallback).
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — operational lifecycle map (generated-runbook variant)

card.failure_class: Substrate drift via hardcoded snapshots: a consumer pastes 'our packages are [A, B, C]' into a lint or test, the model changes, and the consumer keeps passing while reasoning about a stale world — the single most common drift recurrence vector, tempting at every consumer.
card.engineering_obligation: Consumers derive answers from the live model at use time — a copied-out value is banned; one authoritative answer, every consumer derives it, a model change updates all of them at once.
card.solution_structure: A consumption convention (read at run/lint-time, via the query surface for agents or direct import for tools) codified as a preference order (lint-reads-meta-file > codegen > hand-rolled copy), enforced by a forward-policing lint that fails a test embedding a snapshot of a queryable value, plus a rule that lints declare their scope against the component model rather than hardcoding it.
card.guarantee: No private copies on the policed paths; the consumer's answer is the model's answer. Boundary: the ban-lint must recognize what counts as a queryable value; slight per-consumer ceremony and load-time coupling.
card.semantic_level: consumer value → live model query — single source of truth; the copy relation banned.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A query call instead of a literal (the intended trade). The consumer now depends on the model loading when it runs. The ban-lint's accuracy bounds the guarantee.
card.dependencies: query-surface (the canonical read path); the models themselves; consumed by dynamic-context-injection, coherence-lints, doc-hygiene-lints, the reflection facets (policy by reference).
card.known_uses: DocAble's component registry + repo-query read at runtime by the lint fleet and dispatch; the snapshot-ban lint; the lint-scope-declares-against-the-model rule.
card.likely_parent_family: Read the model, don't copy it (canonical pattern)

models-bridge/system-models/model-derive.title: Model-derived test-obligation census (derive obligations, lint the gap)

card.failure_class: Coverage blind to what should exist: whole categories of obligation (an unfuzzed external seam, a failure edge with no injection test, an invariant with no checker) sit at zero behind a rising line-coverage percentage, because coverage's denominator is what you built, not what you owe — and every new seam silently adds an obligation nothing counts.
card.engineering_obligation: Derive the should-be-tested denominator from the models themselves and lint the gap to the tests that exist — an untested obligation is a named, listable finding whose set regrows with every model change.
card.solution_structure: Walk the structured models that declare a testable surface (seam registry, failure-edge model, invariant list) to compute obligation sets; join each obligation against the test corpus (by convention, tag, or registry); an obligation with no matching test is a finding attributable to the model element that generated it; one census genre reused across obligation kinds.
card.guarantee: An entire untested category is a listable finding set, and a newly-added surface reopens the gap until a test closes it. Boundary: measures obligation coverage, not test quality — a matched weak test counts as covered; the obligation↔test join must track naming/tagging or it reports false gaps or false safety.
card.semantic_level: model-declared surface → owed test — the obligation relation, with the denominator drawn from the model rather than the code.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The matching rule is load-bearing maintenance. Quality judgment is delegated to other mechanisms. The census is only as complete as the models that declare surfaces.
card.dependencies: Models declaring testable surfaces (executable-source-of-truth); a matchable test corpus; a gate treating unmet obligations as findings; fuzz-campaigns discharge the fuzz obligations; generalizes coverage-model-mapping across obligation kinds; sibling journey-task-closure.
card.known_uses: DocAble's fuzz-target census (should-be-fuzzed from the seam model); the error-path injection census (should-have-injection from the failure-edge model); the invariant-checker census.
card.likely_parent_family: Model-derived assurance coverage

card.failure_class: A model nothing depends on: if models only describe, nothing breaks when they're wrong, so nothing keeps them right; and separately, a hand-edit to a generated artifact is silently lost on the next regen.
card.engineering_obligation: The model must drive the system, not describe it — real artifacts derived from the model, provenance-marked so hand-edits and staleness are mechanically caught.
card.solution_structure: A family of generators reading the models and emitting real artifacts (network policy, service catalog, env wiring, API docs, wire-contract types, docker, human-readable diagrams), each output carrying a provenance header (emitter + regen path) re-emitted every run, enforced by a provenance lint plus a freshness/drift lint.
card.guarantee: One authoritative source per generated artifact class: change the artifact by changing the model; a hand-edit or stale artifact fails the build. Boundary: only the generated classes — everything else needs parity gates instead.
card.semantic_level: artifact = f(model) — the derivation relation, provenance-marked, with hand-edit detection.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A generator per artifact class to author and keep current with the model schema. Generated files must never be hand-edited (a real constraint). Regen discipline on every model change (the freshness lint catches misses).
card.dependencies: Models rich enough to generate from (service-flow, domain-registries, deployment-topology); the provenance-header lint (doc-hygiene kin); cross-target kin: product mutator-stamps ('the tool records what it produced').
card.known_uses: DocAble's NetworkPolicy, service-catalog, env, web-API-entity, public-API-doc, competitor-catalog, wire-contract, and docker generators; the Mermaid model-visualization generator (even the picture a human reads can't drift).
card.likely_parent_family: Executable source of truth (the generation face)

card.failure_class: Findings graded uniformly wrong: an all-or-nothing gate blocks a one-file commit on a pre-existing finding three subsystems away (agents learn to bypass, the gate stops protecting), or each lint re-implements its own relevance scoping and the logic drifts N ways.
card.engineering_obligation: A finding's severity is a function of the finding AND the change, computed by one central authority against a structured model at check time — the relevance decision owned once, never re-implemented per lint.
card.solution_structure: Lints emit structured findings (site, causing input, machine-readable kind, fix-guidance) and stop deciding relevance; the commit gate loads the component model live in-process and runs one grader over every finding: HARD (site or causing input in the changed set — block, with rendered fix-guidance), SOFT (same component — warn), SILENT (elsewhere — defer to the downstream no-baseline backstop); un-gradable findings fail closed to HARD; the grade is additive-restrictive (can relax, cannot fabricate a block).
card.guarantee: One grading rule holds for every finding and every future lint that emits the contract, with a fail-safe worst case (a grader bug can let a finding slip to the backstop, never invent a spurious block). Boundary: SILENT means deferred, not unchecked — the backstop is required.
card.semantic_level: finding × change → severity via model distance — enforcement relevance as a computed relation over the component model, read at check time.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Centralizing the join gives one grader one blast radius (traded against N drifting private copies). SOFT debt accumulates until a hygiene pass. Whole-tree lint runs cost more per governed commit (a cost-threshold routes expensive lints to self-scoped paths). The structured-finding contract becomes load-bearing.
card.dependencies: component-zone-model (read live at check time — the sharpest model-consumed-to-run-a-mechanism instance); the structured-finding emission contract (pre-existing in the instance); the pre-commit hook as host; meta-model-consumption; a downstream no-baseline gate.
card.known_uses: DocAble's governed-doc pre-commit hook grading whole-tree doc-staleness and index-comprehensiveness findings against the component-and-zone model — fixing the recurring blocked-by-unrelated-stale-findings incident; HARD-by-causation for a commit adding an unindexed doc (site untouched, causing input in the change).
card.likely_parent_family: Model-computed enforcement policy (a model dogfooded to grade a gate) — near the drift/parity + meta-consumption cluster

models-bridge/system-models/process-view.title: Process view (concurrent processes, lanes, racing edges)

card.failure_class: Concurrency folklore: nothing names the set of things that run simultaneously, so the pairs that can collide are unenumerated and unguarded — races invisible until they fire, rare enough to survive every test not looking for them; and when the operator is a memory-less agent, the folklore is simply gone.
card.engineering_obligation: Simultaneity is an explicit, closed view: the concurrent processes, the lanes they run in, and every racing edge over shared state, each joined to the guard that serializes it.
card.solution_structure: Enumerate the running things (not code paths); assign lanes (handler, worker, cron, orchestrator loop); declare racing edges as first-class elements (the two processes + the contended resource); check the edge↔guard join both ways (an unguarded edge and an orphan lock are each build findings); project the view from the machine model and the lock registry — derived, not re-authored.
card.guarantee: Every declared race has a guard and every guard a declared race. Boundary: a projection inherits its sources' fidelity — wrong machine model or lock registry means confidently wrong in the same place.
card.semantic_level: process ∥ process over a shared resource — the simultaneity/collision relation, deliberately distinct from transition legality.
card.forces_tradeoffs: N processes admit up to N² shared-resource pairs — the combinatorial surface folklore was silently under-counting, surfaced. New concurrent processes force the which-can-I-collide-with question at design time.
card.dependencies: composed-state-machine-model (the substrate projected over); synchronization-model (the lock registry read for guards); concurrency-contracts (what many edges resolve to).
card.known_uses: DocAble's Kruchten-style process view: worker/handler/cron/orchestrator lanes; named racing edges (preemption requeue vs stale-sweep, two workers vs one queue entry, progress writer vs terminal archive) each joined to its lock or atomic step.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — concurrency simultaneity view

card.failure_class: Ad-hoc, error-prone model access: left to cat/grep the model files, agents and one-off tools re-implement loading and traversal, get the dialect subtly wrong, and produce brittle one-offs — defeating the queryable map's purpose.
card.engineering_obligation: Provide one canonical, self-describing read API over the models so bounded agents consume structure, not prose, and the loading dialect is documented once.
card.solution_structure: A CLI with ~15 deterministic subcommands and a stable --json contract, plus a self-describing models meta-command; co-located with the models so its loader is the canonical load example; atomic writes where relevant.
card.guarantee: Deterministic structured output on the canonical path. Boundary: soft — the canonical convenience, not a lint-banned monopoly; direct import remains legitimate for Python tools.
card.semantic_level: consumer → model read path — the access relation canonicalized (one documented dialect instead of N re-derivations).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Not the sole path, by design. A subcommand surface that grows with every model added.
card.dependencies: The models loading cleanly (executable-source-of-truth); meta-model-consumption as the discipline it serves; ridden by the traceability graph, the blast-radius query, and the coverage roll-ups.
card.known_uses: DocAble's repo-query CLI (component / service-flow / frontend-flow / design / callers / xrefs / epic / task / web-api / config, --json); the repo-query orchestrator skill.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable source of truth (the agent-facing read face)

card.failure_class: An incomplete environment admitted: the process starts fine and fails only when it reaches the one code path that reads the missing secret — a 403 deep in a request, an inter-service auth failure, a silently-empty GenAI call — late, quiet, far from the cause, once per missing variable.
card.engineering_obligation: Configuration completeness is an admission policy: the full required set per role and plane is declared and checked at the boundary before any work begins — fail loud and early with the whole gap, never late and quiet.
card.solution_structure: A typed manifest keyed by role × plane listing the complete required configuration set; an admission check compares the environment at start-up and refuses to launch on any missing entry, reporting the entire gap at once; the declared set reconciled against what each role's code actually reads.
card.guarantee: An incomplete environment is refused at the door with the full missing list. Boundary: presence, not validity — a wrong-but-set key passes admission and fails at use.
card.semantic_level: runtime environment ⊇ role's declared required set — completeness as an admission relation, per role and plane.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The manifest is another surface (the reconciliation gate forces code and manifest to agree). Only per-site reads can never assert completeness — that property exists only at the declared-set level.
card.dependencies: role-typed-dispatch (the role the manifest keys by); an admission point (start-up hook, dispatch gate); drift-parity-gates (reconciliation against real reads); meta-model-consumption (the check reads the manifest).
card.known_uses: DocAble's dispatch-role × plane required-env manifest with the start-up admission gate; the reconciliation against real getenv sites.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — admission-completeness manifest

card.failure_class: A governance document opaque to programs: aggregate questions (which rules have automated enforcers? which govern this subtree? which are blocking?) are manual whole-document reads done from memory that rot with rule count — and a rule can claim an enforcing lint that no longer exists with nothing noticing.
card.engineering_obligation: Governance rules carry machine-readable metadata, extracted into a typed queryable registry whose claims are cross-checked against the real enforcers — the policy corpus becomes a model.
card.solution_structure: A structured metadata block inside each rule (stable id, scope, severity, enforcing check, canonical detail pointer), co-located with the prose; a build step extracts the blocks into a typed registry; cross-checks flag a rule citing a missing enforcer or a dangling detail pointer as build findings.
card.guarantee: The document's enforcement claims stay reconciled with the enforcing system; aggregate questions are registry queries. Boundary: a stale block asserting a gone guarantee is worse than none — the cross-check exists for exactly this.
card.semantic_level: governance rule → its enforcement + scope metadata — the rule's claim ⟷ the real enforcer; policy prose made queryable.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Every rule owes a well-formed block (authoring cost, made mandatory by the reconciliation gate). The prose stays for humans; the block serves the tooling.
card.dependencies: claude-md-rule-index (the document-side twin this extracts the model from); domain-registries sibling; query-surface exposes it; drift-parity-gates.
card.known_uses: DocAble's inline rule-meta blocks on the numbered project rules; the extracted typed rule registry; the enforcer/pointer cross-checks.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — governance-metadata registry (governance-of-governance leaning)

card.failure_class: SOA facts (inter-service auth, URLs, NetworkPolicy, the deploy table, API contracts, frontend trees) restated across code + YAML + deploy scripts drift apart — an endpoint the NetworkPolicy doesn't allow, a handler diverged from its spec, a tree with no entity — each a production-shaped bug across many surfaces.
card.engineering_obligation: One source of truth for the service architecture, from which the real wiring is generated and against which reality is bidirectionally parity-checked — nothing left to hand-sync.
card.solution_structure: A Backstage-dialect entity model (Component/API/System with org annotations) plus OpenAPI, wire-contract, and config schemas; generators emit NetworkPolicy, service catalog, env wiring, and API docs from it; bidirectional drift lints (frontend tree ↔ entity both ways, handler ↔ spec, call-graph ↔ model).
card.guarantee: Neither the model nor reality drifts unilaterally on the modeled surfaces; a new service/endpoint/tree is a model edit or a parity failure — deliberately.
card.semantic_level: service topology + API contracts ⟷ deployed reality — the structural who-exists-and-how-wired relation of the architecture.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Dialect lock-in (the deliberate adopt-the-canonical-schema trade). Generator and gate maintenance across several surfaces.
card.dependencies: model-driven-codegen (its generation face); drift-parity-gates; query-surface; serves as the shared carrier the user-journey kind grafts onto.
card.known_uses: DocAble's Backstage-dialect service YAML as the SOA source of truth; the NetworkPolicy/catalog/env/API-doc generation; the tree↔yaml and handler↔spec parity lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — structural service architecture (a flagship known-use of Executable Source of Truth)

card.failure_class: Silent traceability rot: the cross-references an agent walks between abstraction levels (model → enforcing lint → code root → proof → registry) go stale on every refactor — the model still looks authoritative while pointing at a ghost, and the blow-up lands days later in a downstream gate; plus the pointer-drift class (a built replacement never repointed-to, so the system defaults to the retired implementation).
card.engineering_obligation: Every cross-layer join is a typed, derived edge re-provable against live reality — derived edges defend, snapshotted ones drift; liveness must be a property of the representation (resolution IS the read), not a sync process running beside a snapshot.
card.solution_structure: A typed graph: TraceEdges over a closed kind vocabulary (governs / enforced-by / verified-by / derived-from / points-at) with a sanctioned kind-pair table and a non-optional derivation per edge, each terminating on a SymbolAnchor (path, symbol, resolver — never a line number; resolver chosen by file type, textual fallback only as a declared weak edge); a meta-lint re-derives every edge at DoD/audit cadence (cost-bound); an active-implementation registry + pointer-agreement lint for the points-at class; bidirectional traversal doubles as the agent's externalized mental model; an unresolvable anchor routes as an abstraction-completeness finding (the code lacks the seam), not an error.
card.guarantee: A broken join reddens at scan time, and an anchor that resolves means both the model's claim is currently true and the agent's traversal is a current slice. Boundary: resolution catches deletion, not demotion (a symbol that exists but no longer plays the claimed role resolves green — the keyword companion covers role currency); cadence, not per-commit.
card.semantic_level: model element ⟷ its enforcing/verifying/governed artifacts — the join web between abstraction levels, held by derivation rather than storage.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Symbol resolution is expensive — the cadence follows the cost. Weak-prover fallbacks are standing flagged debt. The closed edge vocabulary must evolve honestly (no untyped string edges).
card.dependencies: Existing static symbol resolvers (the graph composes them); structured models with addressable elements; in-situ anchor homes (typed fields, structured comment trailers); query-surface for bidirectional walks; generalizes drift-parity-gates beyond the single model↔code edge kind.
card.known_uses: DocAble's trace graph: a twelve-model fan-out classifying ~600 anchors caught ~14 genuine drifts for which NO existing lint fired (near-1 signal-to-noise, zero false positives); the clean-vs-drifted split evidence (anchor-linted models drifted zero; unlinted registries carried the drift); the active-implementation registry seeded by a prod-blocking unwired-replacement incident; the proof-as-anchor trajectory (a verified-by edge targeting a checker run, enabling triggered re-verification).
card.likely_parent_family: Drift/parity gate (generalized: the derived traceability graph over the whole join web) — possibly its own canonical pattern
card.note: Strong canonical-pattern candidate in its own right ('Derived Traceability'); the entry's evidence discipline (designed from observed drift, validated on an independent drift set) is unusually strong.

card.failure_class: Undeclared locks and inverted acquisition orders: nobody can answer which locks exist, what each guards, or in what order they must be taken — so a deadlock-inducing ordering can only be suffered at runtime, and the hazard recurs with every lock added.
card.engineering_obligation: Every synchronization primitive, the resource it guards, and the required acquisition ordering is declared and checkable before the code runs — concurrency contracts as data, not tribal knowledge.
card.solution_structure: Three typed records — SyncLock (path, cap, model, bypass-env, audit-log), LockAcquirer (each declared acquisition site, or none-with-rationale), LockOrdering (before/after with rationale); a coverage lint scans the real flock/lockf call sites and requires each declared or explicitly annotated; an ordering lint walks the declared orderings + call graph to catch inverted acquisition.
card.guarantee: An undeclared lock and an inverted acquisition each fail at author time. Boundary: a missing ordering edge lets a real inversion through — the graph must be maintained.
card.semantic_level: lock → guarded resource + acquisition order — the synchronization-contract relation.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Every new lock is a registry entry (deliberate). The exempt-rationale set is a small carve-out surface.
card.dependencies: The agent mediators acquire these locks (bridge to the mediators family); drift-parity-gates; process-view reads it to join racing edges to guards; the governance graph generalizes its ordering analysis to non-lock slots.
card.known_uses: DocAble's synchronization registry over the dev-time locks (test-serializer flock, build semaphore, lint mutex, commit-slave serializer); the sync-coverage and ordering-constraint lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — synchronization contracts

card.failure_class: Absent telemetry misread as a present zero: a metric collected in production but never locally — the developer profiles a slow path, sees the metric flat, and concludes it's cheap; or the stream is collected everywhere except the plane an incident is unfolding in. Coverage gaps written down nowhere.
card.engineering_obligation: Each observability stream's provenance — what emits it, where it lands, and in which environments it is actually collected — is a declared, reconciled fact, so an absent stream is distinguishable from a true zero.
card.solution_structure: A per-stream typed record: origin (the emitting service/path), landing (the sink), and a per-environment coverage vector; reconciled against the real emit points and collector configuration so a stream emitted but uncollected in a declared-covered plane, or collected without a record, is a build finding.
card.guarantee: Declared coverage matches real collection or the gate reddens; a flat metric is classifiable as genuinely zero vs never collected. Boundary: presence, not usefulness — a well-covered useless metric passes.
card.semantic_level: telemetry stream → (origin, landing, per-environment collection) — the observability-coverage relation.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Coverage vectors must track collector reconfiguration or they assert false confidence. Earns its keep only where collection genuinely varies by plane.
card.dependencies: typed-event-bus (many tracked streams are its topics); drift-parity-gates; sibling caused-by-provenance (same provenance discipline, different subject).
card.known_uses: DocAble's per-stream telemetry registry across local/staging/production planes; the emit-vs-collector reconciliation check; absent-vs-zero classification.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — observability-coverage provenance

models-bridge/system-models/timeout-budg.title: Timeout-budget ordering model (nested wall-clock budgets, checked)

card.failure_class: Independently-set wall-clock budgets invert: an inner timeout outlasting the operation that contains it — hangs, leaked locks, retry windows outliving their total budget — visible in no single constant, debugged by reconstructing the intended nesting from scattered numbers.
card.engineering_obligation: The system's temporal budgets are one declared surface with their containment ordering stated and proven — inner strictly expires before outer, for every declared pair, for any future edit.
card.solution_structure: One declared surface holding every budget (request timeouts, worker deadlines, lock waits, retry windows); the nesting relation declared per containing pair; a property test quantifying inner < outer over all pairs; the surface mirroring and reconciled against the authoritative constants the code enforces.
card.guarantee: A budget raised past its container fails at the edit — a latent production hang converted to a build finding. Boundary: proves consistent nesting only, not that any budget is well chosen.
card.semantic_level: inner budget < containing budget — the temporal containment ordering over nested operations.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The nesting relation must be authored (which budget contains which); an unstated nesting is unchecked. Small surface, sharp payoff, deliberately narrow scope.
card.dependencies: A property-test harness (the linear-ordering shape formal-invariant-verification routes to property tests); consumers sourcing budgets from the surface (meta-model-consumption); sibling synchronization-model (lock order vs timeout order).
card.known_uses: DocAble's pipeline wall-clock-budget surface (per-stage deadlines, lock waits, retry windows) with the nesting-order property test.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — resource-ordering invariant surface

models-bridge/system-models/typed-contra.title: Typed contract surfaces (checked boundary, not a comment)

card.failure_class: A boundary contract living as a comment, an example payload, or nothing: one side changes shape, the other keeps parsing the old one, and the mismatch surfaces as a runtime error at the far end — an API drops a field, a cross-language status marker is renamed, a CLI's stdout JSON changes and every piping script breaks.
card.engineering_obligation: The contract between two parties is one declared, typed surface that BOTH the real producer and the real consumer reconcile against at build time — and it carries the boundary's policy (visibility, auth, stability), not just its field names.
card.solution_structure: Per boundary genre, an authored typed surface: a structured endpoint model with visibility/auth/billing extensions reconciled against handlers; a cross-language marker-and-JSON wire registry checked against both emit and parse sites; a per-subcommand CLI-output spec whose stable points double as fuzz oracles (an adversarial input fails to the declared spec point, not one run's formatting).
card.guarantee: A breaking change reddens the gate at the edit, not in production at the far side. Boundary: a surface no check reconciles is worse than none — it looks authoritative and lies.
card.semantic_level: producer shape ⟷ declared contract ⟷ consumer expectation — the boundary-shape relation, plus typed boundary policy.
card.forces_tradeoffs: One more surface to keep true (the reconciliation gate is load-bearing). Three boundary genres share the pattern but stay distinct instances — folding them blurs checks that run at different times against different consumers.
card.dependencies: drift-parity-gates (the reconciliation machinery); fuzz-campaigns (consumer of the CLI oracle); service-flow-model sibling (who talks vs in what language); semantic-level-enforcement (check at the boundary's own level, not a string match below).
card.known_uses: DocAble's endpoint model with per-endpoint visibility/auth/billing; the cross-language wire-contract registry (C# worker markers ↔ Python coordinator); the per-subcommand stdout spec used as the fuzz oracle.
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — boundary contract surfaces

card.failure_class: The path from product goal to code lives in heads — the journey is the one thing the code never names: journeys go untested unnoticed, endpoints accrete that no journey needs and no one dares delete, declared dependencies silently fall out of date with real call sites, capacity is sized to a blurred average.
card.engineering_obligation: The traversal from what the product is for to what the code must provide is a queryable, reconciled model — behavioral, goal-anchored entities joined to the endpoints they cross, held fresh by parity.
card.solution_structure: A Journey entity kind (actor · goal · ordered steps, each naming its endpoints, plus call-site anchors) grafted into the existing structural service dialect — distinct model, shared carrier (loader, query, lint machinery inherited); a call-site drift lint holds declared deps ↔ real call sites both directions; two coverage audits ride the model (undertested-journey, dead-endpoint); audit-only → fix-wave → blocking.
card.guarantee: The journey→deps map is a checked cache of the call-site truth (O(1)-at-PR correction instead of O(N)-PRs silent drift). The runtime capability it unlocks (journey-aware differential scale-up) is gated on the drift lint being blocking — capability enabled by the model, made safe by the governance that keeps it true.
card.semantic_level: product goal → implementation surface — a behavioral traversal joined down to structure; declared dependency ⟷ real call site.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The semantic fields (actor, goal, steps) are human-authored — a linted document, not codegen. Journey granularity is an explicit modeling choice (too coarse = toothless audits, too fine = noise). Audit-only-first is the honest landing.
card.dependencies: service-flow-model (the shared carrier); drift-parity machinery; consumed by journey-criticality-test-placement and journey-task-closure; executable-source-of-truth as the pattern instantiated.
card.known_uses: DocAble's typed Journey entities; the two-way call-site drift lint; the dead-endpoint and undertested-journey audits; the journey-aware wake/scale capability; the migration completeness-critic sweep (walking journeys to find the threads a component-deep plan misses).
card.likely_parent_family: Executable-model zoo — goal-anchored behavioral journeys

card.failure_class: Ad hoc tree recursion re-implements traversal at every site, each copy subtly wrong its own way — a missed node type, a wrong order, forgotten link annotations — and a fix to one copy never reaches the others.
card.engineering_obligation: Each tree's traversal invariants live in exactly one walker inherited everywhere — one copy of the traversal to get right.
card.solution_structure: One canonical walker per tree type owning its traversal shape; a discipline (with lint coverage riding the model ban-lints) that routes all traversal through it, banning raw recursion and regex-into-tree.
card.guarantee: The traversal invariants are fixed once. Boundary: a missing traversal shape pushes callers back to raw recursion — coverage matters exactly as for the models.
card.semantic_level: traversal → the canonical walker — uniqueness of the traversal relation per tree (DRY + invariant centralization).
card.forces_tradeoffs: The walker must expose what callers need. Low novelty, acknowledged in the entry — value is centralization, not invention.
card.dependencies: pdf-model and office-models (the structured models walked); the ban-lint coverage.
card.known_uses: DocAble's PdfStructTreeWalker, the RuleWalkers, DocxTopLevelPartWalker.
card.likely_parent_family: One Door Enforced (traversal component) — likely an L3 component of the sanctioned-surface pattern rather than a peer pattern
card.note: Entry self-declares low novelty; strong demotion-to-component candidate for 3b.

card.failure_class: The same raw-library corruption class on a second object model: raw OpenXML SDK access — and the sneakier regex-into-the-serialized-XML path — is brittle and corruption-prone with no single invariant-enforcement point, recurring independently across three document formats.
card.engineering_obligation: Defect-class consolidation: apply the one construction+ban pattern per object model so a fix to the pattern benefits every format at once — capability parity is sufficient justification; the merged path need not be more capable.
card.solution_structure: A structured model per Office format plus a shared common layer; the checking layer routed through canonical rule walkers; two ban-lints — one on the raw SDK, one on raw-XML string-matching (closing the escape a plain no-raw-SDK rule misses).
card.guarantee: The corruption class is killed uniformly across formats. Boundary: per-format coverage gaps force noqa or extension; the string-match ban can false-positive on legitimate document-text operations.
card.semantic_level: every mutation → the sanctioned typed seam — the same one-door relation, instantiated on a second object model (the consolidation is the point).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Three models plus a shared layer — more surface than the single-format seam. Escape hatches needed for string-match false positives.
card.dependencies: Sibling pdf-model (the unified pattern); the two ban-lints; canonical-walkers (RuleWalkers).
card.known_uses: DocAble's SlidesModel / DocsModel / SheetsModel + OpenXmlCommon; the openxml-direct-access and no-raw-xml-string-match lints.
card.likely_parent_family: One Door Enforced — instance (the defect-class-consolidation sibling of pdf-model; 3b should fold both as known-uses of one pattern)

card.failure_class: The raw format library is a minefield of silent, invisible-at-the-call-site failures: a forgotten modification-flag call silently drops the write on save; a direct tag/dict mutation corrupts the structure tree (the v172 corruption class). With no single enforcement point, the same bug class recurs at every scattered raw call.
card.engineering_obligation: All mutation of a hazardous format flows through one typed surface that encodes the format's invariants, with the raw alternative structurally banned — the bug made unrepresentable, not reviewed for.
card.solution_structure: A structured model (read via one entry point; write via typed mutators that cannot forget the modification-flag discipline and that wire stamp emission by construction) plus a ban-lint failing the build on any raw constructor or dangerous raw call; the underlying library version pinned, upgrades gated behind a regression suite.
card.guarantee: On the sanctioned path the defect class is unrepresentable; the ban-lint keeps every call site on the path. Boundary: a missing operation forces a noqa hole or a model extension — an incomplete seam weakens the ban.
card.semantic_level: every mutation → the sanctioned typed seam — the one-door relation over a format's mutation surface (construction, held by a counted detection sensor).
card.forces_tradeoffs: The model must cover everything callers need. Version lock-in makes upgrades deliberate gated work. The mutators + ban-lint are a real maintenance surface.
card.dependencies: The ban-lint (a member of the semantic-lint fleet); canonical-walkers for traversal; mutator-stamps wired per verb; remediation-verbs (the same Primitives layer as the closed verb set).
card.known_uses: DocAble's PdfModel.Read + typed Primitives mutators; the raw-library ban-lints; the v172 /StructTreeRoot corruption as the retired defect class.
card.likely_parent_family: One Door Enforced (sanctioned mutation surface) — instance
card.abstract_name: Sole typed mutation surface with raw-path ban

card.failure_class: Scattered raw shared-state calls break two invariants at once: atomicity (a two-command pop-and-move silently loses a job if the worker crashes between them) and schema (key names drift from the declared set, so a depth metric misses a structure).
card.engineering_obligation: Dangerous shared-state operations are encoded once in a sole seam that also owns the declared schema — there is no other place to write the bug.
card.solution_structure: One module as the sole raw-client surface; all queue keys declared in its schema; atomic pop-and-move encoded once (Lua EVAL for sorted sets, RPOPLPUSH for lists), never two commands; a sole-seam lint banning raw access elsewhere.
card.guarantee: Atomicity and schema invariants hold because they have exactly one home; 'a depth metric must query ALL queue structures' becomes enforceable at all. Boundary: the seam must keep pace with new structures or callers are tempted back.
card.semantic_level: every raw-client call → the sole seam — operation ⊨ atomicity + schema invariants encoded once.
card.forces_tradeoffs: A coupling point that must cover every queue operation. Transitional re-export shim debt.
card.dependencies: The sole-seam lint; sibling service-client (same bounded-service pattern).
card.known_uses: DocAble's dispatch module + queue-key schema; the atomic Lua/RPOPLPUSH primitives; the sole-raw-Redis-seam lint.
card.likely_parent_family: One Door Enforced (shared-state seam variant)

card.failure_class: File-path-over-wire type confusion: a cross-service call passes a path string where bytes were meant, and the receiving service in another container cannot open the sender's filesystem — recurring wherever someone reaches for the raw HTTP library.
card.engineering_obligation: Cross-boundary calls flow through one typed seam whose SIGNATURE makes the bug class unrepresentable — the type is the enforcement, applied at a service boundary.
card.solution_structure: A sole typed client whose file-posting signature takes a binary stream (a path is a type error, not a runtime bug); the IPC module is the lint-enforced sole cross-service-HTTP surface; direct raw HTTP against another service is banned.
card.guarantee: The type-confusion class is unrepresentable on the sanctioned path. Boundary: the one client must cover every HTTP shape callers need — a coupling point and evolution bottleneck.
card.semantic_level: every cross-service call → the typed sole seam — the boundary's wire semantics (bytes, not path) encoded in the signature.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Slight ceremony (open a handle rather than pass a path — the point). The seam is a bottleneck for new call patterns.
card.dependencies: The sole-seam lint; sibling raw-redis-seam (same bounded-service pattern on another boundary).
card.known_uses: DocAble's ServiceClient.post_file(BinaryIO); the IPC sole-seam lint; the eliminated file-path-over-wire class.
card.likely_parent_family: One Door Enforced (typed distributed variant)

card.failure_class: Untracked or mislabelled inserted content: tool-inserted scaffolding presented as if the author wrote it, or an insert that isn't tracked and therefore isn't validated — recurring per inserter and per insertion site; ad-hoc naming and hand-maintained lists both fail because neither is checkable.
card.engineering_obligation: Tool-inserted content is distinguishable from authored content by a checkable rule, and every inserter is automatically covered by validation through registration — marking plus auto-coverage, mechanical rather than promised.
card.solution_structure: A three-way naming rule (invisible insert → reserved prefix; user-visible insert → ordinary name; spec-mandated → the spec name) plus a registry every new inserter records into, read by an inserted-content validator that covers registered inserts automatically; off-canvas placement uses dynamic geometry so scaffolding never bleeds on-page.
card.guarantee: Registered inserts are validator-covered by construction. Boundary: adherence is partly discipline — a mis-named or unregistered insert escapes until caught; spec-name exceptions are a tracked carve-out.
card.semantic_level: inserted artifact → declared origin marking — the authored-vs-tool-inserted distinction made checkable by rule.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The auto-coverage only works if the registration habit holds. The prefix rule needs its spec-mandated exception class.
card.dependencies: The insert registry + InsertedContentValidator; sibling remediation-verbs (bounding how inserts happen); part of the provenance stack (marking the insertions the stamps attribute).
card.known_uses: DocAble's a11y_ prefix convention + per-site corollaries; registry.Record(...) + the InsertedContentValidator.
card.likely_parent_family: Complete mutation provenance (the durable insertion-marking component)
card.abstract_name: Durable insertion marking with registered validation coverage

card.failure_class: Attribution present but inert: the stamps are embedded in the artifact but without a reader the evidence cannot be assembled into 'pass X made change Y' — surfacing exactly when someone needs the history for RCA or user transparency.
card.engineering_obligation: Provenance must have a consumer: the attributed history is reconstructable from the artifact on demand — no reader, no reason to stamp.
card.solution_structure: A command reading the embedded stamp registry and emitting a ChangeLog (each entry a mutation attributed to its pass, with its visibility), run after remediation against the produced artifact.
card.guarantee: A reproducible, attributed reconstruction — answering what a raw input-vs-output diff cannot (who, and why). Boundary: only as complete as the stamps (an attribution gap becomes a hole in the history); schema-coupled to the stamp registry.
card.semantic_level: embedded provenance → reconstructed attributed history — the read side of the in-artifact provenance relation.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Depends on stamp-schema stability across versions.
card.dependencies: mutator-stamps (hard dependency); f10-wiring-lint (guarantees the completeness the reader relies on).
card.known_uses: DocAble's derive-changelog command (stamp registry → ChangeLog JSON per pass with visibility).
card.likely_parent_family: Complete mutation provenance (the consumer component)

card.failure_class: One new mutator verb added without stamp wiring silently produces unattributable mutations — a hole in the audit trail invisible until an RCA hits it, because a missing call shouts nothing in a diff and is forgotten exactly under time pressure.
card.engineering_obligation: Completeness of provenance coverage over the closed verb set is mechanically guaranteed — pitch the check at 'was the call made on the way out', the level where completeness is legible AND cheap, not at 'was the work correct', where no lint could decide.
card.solution_structure: A blocking lint scanning the document models' Primitives directories for mutator verbs and asserting each calls the stamp wiring; a gap is a HIGH-severity build failure; the invariant held at 0 open gaps.
card.guarantee: No verb lands unwired — 'we attribute mutations' becomes a guarantee, not an aspiration. Boundary: the verb-detection heuristic is the weak point (miss a shape → a real gap passes; over-match → false failures); coupled to the Primitives layout.
card.semantic_level: every mutation verb → wired provenance emission — the coverage-completeness relation over the provenance stack (distinct from parity and from semantic policy, though the technology is a lint).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Cheap by construction because it checks control-flow order, not behavior. A Primitives reorganization needs the lint updated in step.
card.dependencies: mutator-stamps (the construction it counts); the closed verb set (the finite denominator); a member of the semantic-lint fleet doing a completeness job; an instance of semantic-level-enforcement's pitch-the-guarantee move.
card.known_uses: DocAble's mutator-stamp wiring lint (F10, BLOCKING, held at 0 open gaps).
card.likely_parent_family: Complete mutation provenance (the coverage sensor component)

card.failure_class: Anonymous mutations: when a remediated document comes out wrong, RCA across many passes and four formats is guesswork — you can see the output is wrong but not which pass wrote it or why; logs scroll away and were never attached to the artifact.
card.engineering_obligation: Every mutation carries durable attribution embedded in the artifact at the mutation site, emitted through one sanctioned writer per format, with a visibility policy separating debug scaffolding from user-visible record.
card.solution_structure: One sanctioned stamp-writer per format (the raw stamp mutator lint-banned so the helper is the sole surface): a PDF stamp-writer helper and an append-only OOXML attribution registry; visibility Debug by default / Preserved for user-visible passes; a strip step removes Debug stamps before delivery; completeness supplied by the wiring lint.
card.guarantee: The mutation history is reconstructable from the artifact itself, any time. Boundary: stamps add document overhead (stripped pre-delivery); completeness is only guaranteed jointly with the F10 lint.
card.semantic_level: every mutation site → an embedded provenance record — in-artifact attribution at the point of change.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Helper-only discipline (bypass produces un-uniform stamps — lint-guarded). Every new verb must wire it — the cost F10 turns from 'remember' into 'must'.
card.dependencies: f10-wiring-lint (the completeness sensor); derive-changelog (the reader); remediation-verbs (the closed set that makes 'stamp every verb' finite); counterpart caused-by-provenance (agent-side).
card.known_uses: DocAble's MutatorStampHelper.WriteStamp (PDF) and OoxmlAttributionRegistry.AppendEntry (OOXML); the Debug/Preserved model + strip-attribution.
card.likely_parent_family: Complete mutation provenance (the emission component of the provenance stack)

card.failure_class: Behaviour unpinned before structural churn is silently lost, and a doc-derived test drifts from the source it was derived from with no signal — two-sided, recurring before every refactor and at every cited-source edit.
card.engineering_obligation: Characterization pins carry provenance to their cited source, and editing a cited source obliges regenerating the link in the same change — the pin ⟷ source join kept honest.
card.solution_structure: Doc-derived characterization tests each carrying a provenance trailer (audited / source / pins) after the module docstring; a regen tool rebuilds the trailer in the same commit as a cited-source edit; a BLOCKING presence lint and a WARNING freshness lint.
card.guarantee: Every pin is traceable to its source and the trailer's presence is enforced. Boundary: freshness is informational only (a stale trailer can linger); near-zero defect yield is the success condition — these pin correct behaviour before change, they don't hunt bugs.
card.semantic_level: test ⟷ cited source — provenance of the characterization pin (parity applied to the tests-derived-from-docs join).
card.forces_tradeoffs: A small per-edit regen cost on cited sources. Low defect yield by design — misread as failure by anyone grading on find-rate.
card.dependencies: A characterization convention + trailer schema; the regen tool; presence/freshness lints.
card.known_uses: DocAble's *_doc_derived test files with DDT-audited/DDT-source/DDT-pins trailers; the trailer regenerator; the blocking presence lint.
card.likely_parent_family: Drift/parity gate (test ⟷ cited-source variant) — with a provenance-discipline face

card.failure_class: Crashes and corruption on adversarial or spec-edge inputs no hand-written test anticipates — truncated streams, odd encodings, legal-but-unusual structures — hiding in an input space far too large to enumerate; and the production-shaped version: a real user's file from a tool you never tested.
card.engineering_obligation: Falsify the specification with wild inputs, fix to the stable point in the spec (never the failing seed), and measure what the campaign actually reached.
card.solution_structure: Fuzz harnesses + automatic coverage collection against a baseline + the RCA-to-spec discipline; sharpened by two moves: the producer-dialect corpus (real independent third-party producers of the format supply legal-but-unusual dialects, occupying the whole spec-allowed producer space) and fuzz+MBE, where the structured model IS the oracle (wild inputs judged against the model's closed legal-outcome set / invariant predicates — extending to interleaving-fuzz over concurrency invariants).
card.guarantee: Reach is measured, not assumed; with the model-as-oracle the rich-oracle-vs-wild-input tradeoff disappears and a fix aimed at the model's stable point closes every spec-allowed input. Boundary: compute-heavy; seed-fixing is the anti-pattern the RCA discipline exists to prevent.
card.semantic_level: adversarial input → declared stable spec point — falsification against the specification, with the structured model as the declared oracle in the deepest form.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Campaign compute cost; baseline re-basing only on intentional coverage-shape changes; the producer corpus needs real third-party producers.
card.dependencies: typed-contract-surfaces (the CLI-output spec as one oracle); the structured document models (the model-as-oracle); coverage collector + baseline; sibling property-tests (the same generative move, opposite trade).
card.known_uses: DocAble's fuzz/campaign harnesses + auto-coverage; the fix-to-spec RCA discipline; the producer-dialect corpus from rival office suites/PDF writers/converters; the model-as-oracle read-entry fuzzing and the interleaving/simworld concurrency variant.
card.likely_parent_family: Generative validation (fuzz pole; the model-as-oracle synthesis is the distinctive canonical contribution)

card.failure_class: Bugs living in the untested input space: example tests only check the cases someone thought of, and the bug is almost always in the case no one wrote — recurring for any invariant-shaped contract hand-picked examples under-cover.
card.engineering_obligation: Invariant-shaped contracts (round-trip, idempotence, combinatorial laws) are verified over machine-generated inputs, with failures shrunk to minimal counterexamples.
card.solution_structure: Property-based tests declaring rich oracles (the invariants) over tame generated inputs; generators for domain types; shrinking on failure; added per class when a property-shaped contract exists.
card.guarantee: Raises confidence by sampling a space examples never reach — not proof (the exhaustive complement is the model-checking mechanism). Boundary: a wrongly-stated invariant yields false confidence; nondeterministic properties flake.
card.semantic_level: declared invariant over a generated input space — specification falsification at the rich-oracle / tame-input pole of the generative-validation family.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Generators are real work for rich domain types. The property must be a true function of the input.
card.dependencies: FsCheck + generators; the structured models (round-trip properties pin their read/write invariants); the fuzz pole as the same move with the opposite trade.
card.known_uses: DocAble's FsCheck.Xunit round-trip and combinatorial properties across the test projects.
card.likely_parent_family: Generative validation (property pole) — pairs with fuzz-campaigns as one family; standard practice, agentic delta thin
card.note: The entry itself frames property-testing and fuzzing as 'two sides of one coin'; 3b should likely merge into one generative-validation pattern with two poles.

card.failure_class: 4000+ tests are too slow per change but skipping lets regressions land: unstratified you get unusably slow iteration (run everything) or missed regressions (run nothing) — a constant tension at every change and deploy.
card.engineering_obligation: Verification cost is stratified to match the decision being gated — each tier sized to its decision — with escalation rules closing the fixed-subset-misses-things gap.
card.solution_structure: Trait/filter-based tiers (a <30s smoke pre-gate, a seconds-fast lite tier, a targeted class filter for the edit loop, the full ~4min tier at deploy); a 1-second rule for new pre-deploy tests; named high-blast-radius surfaces (runners, validators, registries, prompt constants) that force the full tier before 'done'.
card.guarantee: Each decision is gated at its price. Boundary: tier assignment is judgment (one mis-tiered slow test erodes the tier's promise); escalation depends on agents honoring it.
card.semantic_level: test → cost tier matched to the gated decision — the verification-economics relation over the regression body.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The full tier's ~4min is the deliberate deploy price. Lite bloat is the standing hazard the 1-second rule polices.
card.dependencies: A trait/filter system; the deploy stair (staged-deploy-gates runs the full tier); siblings property-tests / fuzz-campaigns / ddt-pin-trailers.
card.known_uses: DocAble's Suite=Smoke / Suite=Lite / targeted / Format= tiers; the 1-second rule; the Tier-3 escalation surfaces.
card.likely_parent_family: Cost-stratified regression body — standard practice with an agentic escalation-discipline twist; a breadth entry, likely L3
card.note: Nearest exclusion-criterion-2 territory (standard practice); the agentic delta is the escalation rules + 1-second discipline under fleet velocity.

card.failure_class: N inconsistent hand-or-agent fixes for what is actually one deterministic transform: a 200-site mechanical backlog dispatched to 200 agents is 200 chances to diverge (plus expense); hand-editing is slow and inconsistent.
card.engineering_obligation: A large mechanical change with a deterministic fix shape executes as one reviewable transform — the execution mode of bulk change is bounded by a threshold rule; per-site judgment still goes to per-site agents.
card.solution_structure: A threshold discipline (N≳50 sites + deterministic shape → author one AST-level transformer; genuine per-site judgment → agent per site); a pre-commit-skip protocol for codemod-class commits (lint stanza skipped with a reasoned marker, unit tier still runs); finished codemods retained as deprecated reference exemplars.
card.guarantee: None hard — a soft discipline; but the transform it produces is itself deterministic and applied identically everywhere, in one reviewable artifact.
card.semantic_level: mechanical change class → a single deterministic transform — bounding how bulk change executes (an execution-mode vocabulary, not an artifact relation).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Upfront transformer cost pays off only at scale (the threshold encodes this). The lint-stanza skip is a scoped, marker-audited hole. Only for deterministic shapes.
card.dependencies: An AST toolkit; the pre-commit-skip protocol; the deprecated-exemplar retention convention; the agent fleet's own mechanical backlogs as the cross-target face.
card.known_uses: DocAble's N≳50 codemod threshold; the inline-import hoisting codemod; pre-commit-skip markers; codemods kept as paste-ready exemplars.
card.likely_parent_family: Bounded change-execution discipline — process-discipline entry, likely L3 under closed-action-vocabulary or the agent-side work-execution family
card.note: Soft process discipline rather than an artifact mechanism; sits uneasily in the product role — flag for 3b placement.

card.failure_class: Free-form document editing is unbounded: any pass could do anything, and an unbounded edit cannot be stamped, validated, or policy-checked as a set — 'is every mutation stamped? every insert validated? all moves on-policy?' are unanswerable over an open move-space.
card.engineering_obligation: The actor's move-space is a closed, named, typed verb set — bounding the action space is what makes attribution, validation, and policy tractable at all.
card.solution_structure: The document models' Primitives mutators as the sanctioned verb set; a masked-pass architecture routing all change through them; every verb wires its stamp (F10) and, if it inserts, registers with the inserted-content registry; nothing mutates outside the set.
card.guarantee: The move-space is enumerable, so per-move governance questions are finite and answerable. Boundary: a needed action absent from the set forces adding a verb — intended friction that keeps the space closed.
card.semantic_level: every mutation ∈ the closed verb vocabulary — the bounded action space over the artifact.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The verb set grows with remediation capability — a maintenance surface, deliberately.
card.dependencies: Enabler of mutator-stamps and content-validator (finite denominators); coincides with the pdf-model/office-models Primitives layer (the same construction seen as vocabulary rather than seam).
card.known_uses: DocAble's Primitives verb sets across the document models; the masked-pass architecture; per-verb stamp + registration wiring.
card.likely_parent_family: Closed action vocabulary (canonical pattern)

card.failure_class: Bare failure strings: a typo compiles and mis-routes, a switch silently misses a case, a new category isn't forced into every handler — and 'are all categories handled?' cannot even be asked, because an open string set has no edges to check against.
card.engineering_obligation: Enumerable identifier spaces are closed typed sets whose handling is exhaustively checkable, with external strings mapped in at a controlled boundary.
