card.solution_structure: Typed enums replacing free-form strings across producers and consumers; enum-value comparison instead of regex-on-strings; exhaustive-match discipline so a new case lights up every non-exhaustive handler; boundary mapping for external/serialized strings (LLM output, wire formats).
card.guarantee: An unhandled case is a compile-time signal; the category space is enumerable. Boundary: adding a category touches every handler — the point, but real work; the boundary seam still receives strings.
card.semantic_level: category value ∈ closed typed set — a closed vocabulary over a decision space, with exhaustiveness as the checkable property.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Handler-touch cost on category addition. Boundary translation is a permanent seam.
card.dependencies: Compiler exhaustiveness signals; the precondition for error-path enumeration as a testing strategy; cross-target twin: the event bus's const-string topic registry.
card.known_uses: DocAble's ViolationCategory / FailureCategory enums; enum-value comparison per the regex-usage discipline.
card.likely_parent_family: Closed action vocabulary (category variant)

card.failure_class: Cross-source drift: paired sources each individually valid but jointly disagreeing — the canonical case being a new config field missing from the sample JSON that defaults to false at deserialization and silently collapses batching in prod; invisible to any per-file check.
card.engineering_obligation: Relational invariants between independent sources are asserted as first-class checks — the relation itself (subset, equality, one-to-one) is what is linted.
card.solution_structure: Lints that read two or more sources at once and assert a declared consistency relation (config fields ⊆ sample; registry keys = consumer keys; enum cases = handler cases), with companion deserialization tests pinning the same relation; meta-files read at lint time, never snapshotted.
card.guarantee: Registered relations cannot silently diverge. Boundary: an unpaired source that should agree with another is unchecked until someone declares the relation; a wrong relation yields false failures or false confidence.
card.semantic_level: source A ⟷ source B — a declared consistency relation between product artifacts (kin of model↔reality parity, applied across sources).
card.forces_tradeoffs: The lint couples to all its sources' shapes. Pair registration is the coverage boundary.
card.dependencies: Machine-readable paired sources; sibling semantic-lints (per-source complement); cross-target kin meta-model-consumption.
card.known_uses: DocAble's config-field ⊆ sample lints + ConfigDeserialization_* tests; registry-agreement lints.
card.likely_parent_family: Drift/parity gate (cross-source relational variant)

card.failure_class: A mutating pipeline silently drops or alters user content — a deleted paragraph, a mangled table, a lost caption — and the output looks fine while quietly not being what the author wrote: the worst outcome for a fidelity-critical tool, recurring on every pass.
card.engineering_obligation: Preservation is a deterministic post-condition checked on every production artifact — the input's content must survive as a subset of the output's — with a localization variant that names the offending stage.
card.solution_structure: A fidelity gate that extracts the input's content and asserts input ⊆ output mechanically, failing the job in production on violation; a staging-only per-pass variant emits a dedicated marker + nonzero exit identifying which pass dropped content.
card.guarantee: No job delivers with detected content loss; 'content was lost somewhere' becomes 'pass N lost it' in staging. Boundary: everything rests on the extractor and the subset semantics — lossy extraction or un-normalized reordering produces false positives/negatives.
card.semantic_level: input content ⊆ output content — the preservation invariant over the artifact.
card.forces_tradeoffs: Subset semantics are subtle (reordering/whitespace normalization or the gate cries wolf). Runs on every job — the accepted price of the guarantee.
card.dependencies: A comparable content extraction; the post-remediation pre-delivery run point; per-pass hooks; the closed verb set (a bounded move-space makes 'validate every outcome' finite).
card.known_uses: DocAble's ContentValidator production gate; the staging per-pass fidelity marker; the never-drop-authored-content policy it enforces.
card.likely_parent_family: Preservation Invariant (canonical pattern)

card.failure_class: Structural drift quietly reintroducing defect classes: hundreds of domain invariants (no silent catch, no banned API, every boundary call through its seam) that all compile fine and look normal in review — no reviewer can hold hundreds of invariants in mind at fleet velocity.
card.engineering_obligation: Every mechanically-detectable domain invariant is encoded as a blocking check with scoped, reason-bearing escapes — audits become lints; policy moves from reviewer memory to durable machinery.
card.solution_structure: A fleet of self-describing lints (each declaring scope, severity, and a verb-of-checking docstring), BLOCKING ones failing the build, escapes via scoped noqa-with-reason; the fleet sits atop a maxed-out commodity static-analysis floor rather than replacing it; AUDIT-ONLY → BLOCKING migration for new lints.
card.guarantee: Encoded invariants hold at every commit/deploy. Boundary: only what is expressible as a check joins; hundreds of lints are a real maintenance surface; a checker can itself become the hazard (the ReDoS field note — the fix was deleting the regex surface, not linting the bug class).
card.semantic_level: implementation ⊨ semantic policy — per-source domain invariants over the tool's own code (a distinct relation from parity, provenance-coverage, and seam-mediation, even though all use lint technology).
card.forces_tradeoffs: Large maintenance surface (the 500+ magnitude). False positives need audited escape holes. The custom fleet only earns its keep atop the commodity floor.
card.dependencies: A lint framework with declaration discipline; gate wiring; the ban-lints of the canonical-seams family are members of this fleet.
card.known_uses: DocAble's lint-banned-apis, no-silent-catch, console-singleton-mutation, the typed-seam ban-lints; the runnable governance-lint starter example shipped with the catalogue.
card.likely_parent_family: Machine-enforced semantic policy (the blocking-lint fleet as pattern)

card.failure_class: An unfounded conformance claim: the tool ships a document claiming conformance while missing success criteria, or runs checks tied to no standard — 'we check X' never maps to 'we close clause Y'; recurring per document and per new check.
card.engineering_obligation: Conformance is a deterministic predicate in which every finding names the external-standard clause it closes, and the coverage claim is kept honest (covered / gap / aspirational) by a same-commit discipline.
card.solution_structure: A rule engine whose findings map to the exact external success criteria (the standards-mapping step); canonical walkers produce findings over the structured models; a scope doc as the source of truth for in/out-of-scope criteria, updated in the same commit as any gap-closing check; a staging per-pass gate surfacing new findings per pass.
card.guarantee: The conformance claim is auditable clause by clause, not an opaque score. Boundary: only as complete as the mapped checks — unmapped criteria are named gaps, which is the scope doc's whole job.
card.semantic_level: finding → external-standard clause — the artifact ⊨ an external conformance specification, clause-grounded.
card.forces_tradeoffs: The mapping must track standard revisions. Per-pass rule-fail is staging-only. Honesty about gaps is a maintained discipline.
card.dependencies: canonical-walkers (the finding producers); the WCAG-gap domain registry; the scope-doc same-commit rule; layer with content-validator (fidelity + conformance as the two artifact gates).
card.known_uses: DocAble's CheckRunner.ComputeStandards finding→SC mapping over WCAG 2.1 AA / Section 508 / PDF-UA; the staging per-pass rule-engine marker; the WCAG-scope-mapping doc.
card.likely_parent_family: Conformance-to-external-spec engine (clause-grounded validation)
